question.en: Select the synonym of Reluctant. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Reluctant [अनिच्छुक, हिचकिचाने वाला] means unwilling and slow to act. Hesitant is the closest meaning.

Option meanings
Willing — ready to do something [इच्छुक]
Hesitant — unsure and slow to act [झिझकने वाला]
Prompt — done quickly, without delay [तत्पर, शीघ्र]
Eager — strongly wanting to do something [उत्सुक]

Related words: Reluctant: unwilling, disinclined, averse.

question.en:
Choose the option that best describes the meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence:
The new recruit's explanation was a plausible excuse which the manager fell for. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Plausible [विश्वसनीय लगने वाला, तर्कसंगत] means seeming reasonable or believable. The manager accepted the excuse, so it sounded reasonable.

Option meanings
unbelievable — impossible to believe [अविश्वसनीय]
dangerous — likely to cause harm [खतरनाक]
imaginative — showing creativity [कल्पनाशील]
reasonable — fair and believable [तर्कसंगत, उचित]

Related words: Plausible: credible, believable, convincing.

question.en:
Choose the option which is similar in meaning to the underlined word.
She was awfully sorry for her behavior. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Before an adjective such as “sorry”, awfully [बहुत, अत्यधिक] is an intensifier meaning “very”. Immensely carries the same degree.

Option meanings
Somewhat — to a moderate degree [कुछ हद तक]
Adequately — sufficiently [पर्याप्त रूप से]
Nominally — in name only [नाममात्र]
Immensely — to a very great degree [अत्यधिक]

[वह अपने व्यवहार के लिए बहुत अधिक खेद में थी।]

Related words: Awfully (intensifier): extremely, terribly, exceedingly.

question.en:
Choose the option which is similar in meaning to the underlined word.
Australian aborigines are dark-skinned people whose descendants came to the continent from Asia about 25,000 years ago. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Descendants [वंशज] are the children, grandchildren and later generations of a person or group. Among the options, Offsprings (standard form: offspring) is the closest.

Option meanings
Successors — people who follow others in a post or role [उत्तराधिकारी]
Offsprings — children or later generations; standard English uses “offspring” for both singular and plural [संतान, वंशज]
Ancestry — one’s forefathers or line of origin [वंश-परंपरा, पूर्वज]
Originally — at first; an adverb, not a noun [मूल रूप से]

Ancestry is nearly the opposite: it points back to forefathers, while descendants point forward.

Related words: Descendants: progeny, posterity, issue.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word:
MALFEASANCE [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Malfeasance [कदाचार, पद का दुरुपयोग] is wrongful or illegal conduct, especially by a public official. Misconduct is the closest synonym.

Option meanings
Negligence — failure to take proper care [लापरवाही]
Fraudulence — deceitfulness; only one kind of wrongdoing [धोखाधड़ी]
Misconduct — improper or wrongful behaviour [कदाचार]
Loyalty — faithfulness [निष्ठा]

Legal usage distinguishes malfeasance (a wrongful act), misfeasance (a lawful act done wrongly) and nonfeasance (failure to act).

Related words: Malfeasance: wrongdoing, misconduct, malpractice.

question.en:
Which word is nearest in meaning to analysis?
"He had a working analysis of mankind's troubles and was a good judge of character." [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Analysis [विश्लेषण] is a detailed study of something in order to understand it. In the sentence, his “working analysis” of mankind’s troubles is his practical examination of them.

Option meanings
Illusion — a false idea or impression [भ्रम]
Doubt — uncertainty [संदेह]
Conclusion — the result reached after thinking [निष्कर्ष]
Examination — careful inspection or study [परीक्षण, जाँच]

Related words: Analysis: study, scrutiny, evaluation.

question.en:
Which word is nearest in meaning to regret?
"The niece's tone was one of distinct regret." [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Regret [खेद, पछतावा] is a feeling of sadness about something that has happened. Sorrow is the nearest meaning.

Option meanings
Joy — great happiness [आनंद]
Sorrow — deep sadness [दुःख]
Celebration — a joyful occasion [उत्सव]
Relief — reassurance after anxiety [राहत]

Related words: Regret: remorse, sorrow, contrition.

question.en:
Choose a word that is similar in meaning to the word in bold.
It is inevitable that mistakes will occasionally occur. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Inevitable [अपरिहार्य, जिसे टाला न जा सके] means certain to happen. Unavoidable is the exact synonym.

Option meanings
Avertible — able to be prevented [टाला जा सकने योग्य]
Avoidable — able to be avoided [परिहार्य]
Doubtful — uncertain [संदिग्ध]
Unavoidable — impossible to avoid [अपरिहार्य]

Avertible and avoidable are opposites of “inevitable”.

Related words: Inevitable: inescapable, certain, unpreventable.

question.en:
Choose a word similar in meaning to the underlined word.
The woman looked wan and fragile. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Wan [पीला, निस्तेज] means pale and weak-looking, as from illness or tiredness. Pallid is the closest meaning.

Option meanings
Flushed — red in the face [लाल, तमतमाया]
Pallid — pale, lacking colour [पीला, फीका]
Agile — quick and nimble [फुर्तीला]
Blooming — healthy and fresh [खिला हुआ, स्वस्थ]

Related words: Wan: pale, ashen, sallow.

question.en: What is the synonym of "Conceal"? [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Conceal [छिपाना] means to keep something from being seen or known. Hide is the synonym.

Option meanings
Reveal — to make known [प्रकट करना]
Hide — to put out of sight [छिपाना]
Display — to show openly [प्रदर्शित करना]
Expose — to uncover [उजागर करना]

Related words: Conceal: hide, cover up, mask.

question.en:
Which word is nearest in meaning to 'demonstrating'?
This trend is already booming in China, demonstrating significant potential globally. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Demonstrating [प्रदर्शित करना, साबित करना] here means clearly showing the trend’s potential to the world. Showcasing — presenting something prominently to a wide audience — fits this global context best.

Option meanings
Exhibiting — showing publicly; also used for displaying objects [प्रदर्शित करना]
Displaying — putting on view [दिखाना]
Showcasing — presenting prominently to show its strength [विशेष रूप से प्रदर्शित करना]
Revealing — making known something hidden [उजागर करना]

Related words: Demonstrating: showing, proving, evidencing.

question.en:
Which word can best replace 'moored' in this context?
The boat was moored at the edge of the island. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Moored [लंगर डाला हुआ, बाँधा हुआ] means fastened in place with ropes or an anchor. Anchored fits the sentence.

Option meanings
Anchored — held in place by an anchor [लंगर डाला हुआ]
Sailed — travelled by boat [नौका से यात्रा की]
Lost — unable to be found [खोया हुआ]
Floated — drifted on water [तैरता रहा]

Related words: Moored: docked, berthed, tied up.

question.en:
Which word can best replace ingenuity?
The ancient Egyptians demonstrated remarkable ingenuity in their architectural designs. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Ingenuity [चतुराई, आविष्कारशीलता] is the quality of being clever and inventive. Creativity is the closest option.

Option meanings
Creativity — the ability to produce original ideas [रचनात्मकता]
Stupidity — lack of intelligence [मूर्खता]
Simplicity — plainness [सरलता]
Ignorance — lack of knowledge [अज्ञानता]

Related words: Ingenuity: inventiveness, resourcefulness, cleverness.

question.en:
Choose the option that best describes the meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence:
Some plants lie dormant throughout the winter. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Dormant [सुप्त, निष्क्रिय] means temporarily inactive, as if asleep.
Its closest meaning is Inert [निष्क्रिय, गतिहीन], lacking the ability to move or act.

Option meanings
Active — engaged in action [सक्रिय]
Full of life — lively, energetic [जीवंत]
Inert — without activity or movement [निष्क्रिय]
Permanent — lasting for ever [स्थायी]

Related words: inactive, latent, quiescent (antonyms: active, awake).

question.en:
Choose the option which is similar in meaning to the underlined word.
She was angry because they disregarded her feelings. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Disregarded [अनदेखा किया] means ignored or paid no attention to.
Among the options, the closest meaning is Unrecognized [जिसे मान्यता या महत्त्व न दिया गया हो]: her feelings were not acknowledged.

Option meanings
Unrecognized — not acknowledged or given attention [अनदेखा, अमान्य]
Acknowledged — accepted or recognised [स्वीकार किया]
Considered — thought about carefully [विचार किया]
Interrupted — stopped in the middle [बाधित किया]

Related words: ignored, overlooked, neglected (antonyms: heeded, respected).

question.en:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word:
OUTLANDISH [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Outlandish [विचित्र, अजीबोगरीब] means looking or sounding very strange or unfamiliar.
Its synonym is Bizarre [विचित्र].

Option meanings
Conventional — following accepted customs [पारंपरिक]
Normal — usual, ordinary [सामान्य]
Bizarre — very strange or unusual [विचित्र]
Predictable — that can be foreseen [पूर्वानुमेय]

Related words: weird, eccentric, peculiar (antonyms: ordinary, conventional).

question.en:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word:
ABJECT [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Abject [अधम, दयनीय, निकृष्ट] describes something extremely bad or a person completely without pride or dignity, e.g. "an abject coward".
Its closest synonym here is Worthless [निकम्मा, तुच्छ].

Option meanings
Rebellious — resisting authority [विद्रोही]
Worthless — having no value or merit [तुच्छ, निकम्मा]
Elevated — raised to a higher level [उन्नत]
Deserving — worthy of something [योग्य]

Related words: wretched, miserable, contemptible (antonyms: proud, dignified).

question.en:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word:
DOLOROUS [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Dolorous [दुःखभरा, पीड़ादायक] means feeling or expressing great sorrow or pain.
Its synonym is Painful [पीड़ादायक].

Option meanings
Joyous — full of happiness [आनंदमय]
Painful — causing pain or sorrow [पीड़ादायक]
Triumphant — rejoicing in victory [विजयी]
Indifferent — having no interest or concern [उदासीन]

Related words: mournful, doleful, woeful (antonyms: cheerful, joyous).

question.en:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word:
DISCONSOLATE [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Disconsolate [अत्यंत उदास, निराश] means very unhappy and impossible to comfort.
Its synonym is Cheerless [उदास, नीरस].

Option meanings
Comforted — made to feel less sad [सांत्वना पाया हुआ]
Joyful — very happy [आनंदित]
Cheerless — gloomy, without joy [उदास]
Excited — very enthusiastic [उत्साहित]

Related words: dejected, forlorn, inconsolable (antonyms: cheerful, contented).

question.en: What is the synonym of "Melancholy"? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Melancholy [उदासी, विषाद] means a deep, long-lasting feeling of sadness.
So its synonym is Sad.

Option meanings
Happy — feeling pleasure [प्रसन्न]
Cheerful — noticeably happy and optimistic [हँसमुख]
Sad — unhappy, sorrowful [दुखी, उदास]
Joyful — full of joy [आनंदित]

Related words: gloomy, sorrowful, despondent (antonyms: cheerful, joyful).

question.en: What is the synonym of "Quaint"? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Quaint [पुराने ढंग का, अनोखा-सा] means attractively unusual or old-fashioned, e.g. "a quaint little village".
So its synonym is Old-fashioned.

Option meanings
Modern — of the present time [आधुनिक]
Old-fashioned — belonging to an earlier time [पुराने ढंग का]
Large — big in size [बड़ा]
Ordinary — common, with nothing special [साधारण]

Related words: charming, picturesque, antiquated (antonym: modern).

question.en: What is the synonym of "Tangible"? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Tangible [मूर्त, ठोस] means something that can be touched, or something real and definite, e.g. "tangible evidence".
Its closest synonym is Concrete (real, solid, existing in physical form).
"Visible" only means able to be seen; something can be visible without being tangible (e.g. a rainbow).

Option meanings
Abstract — existing only as an idea [अमूर्त]
Visible — able to be seen [दृश्य]
Concrete — real, solid, definite [ठोस, मूर्त]
Intangible — that cannot be touched [अमूर्त, अस्पृश्य] (antonym of tangible)

Related words: palpable, physical, substantial, real.

question.en:
Which word is closest in meaning to 'influence' in this context?
Vaynerchuk also highlights the impending influence of AI on content creation, predicting that artificial intelligence will start replacing influencers and podcasters. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Impact [प्रभाव, असर] is the closest meaning. The sentence speaks of the strong, far-reaching influence AI will have on content creation, to the extent of replacing influencers and podcasters.
"Effect" usually means a result, "authority" means the power to command, and "sway" means control over someone, so they fit the context less well.

Option meanings
Impact — a strong effect or influence on something [प्रभाव]
Effect — a change that results from something [परिणाम]
Authority — the power to give orders [अधिकार]
Sway — control or influence over people [प्रभुत्व]

question.en:
Which word is closest in meaning to discarded?
Mitchell Marsh, the discarded all-rounder, is believed to still have the potential to impact the Ashes series against England. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Discarded [त्याग दिया गया] here means left out of the team. In cricket, a player who is left out of the side is said to be dropped [टीम से बाहर किया गया].
So Dropped is the closest meaning in this context.

Option meanings
Rejected — refused or not accepted [अस्वीकृत]
Dropped — left out of a team [टीम से बाहर किया गया]
Abandoned — left completely and permanently [परित्यक्त]
Ignored — deliberately not noticed [उपेक्षित]

question.en:
Which word is nearest in meaning to competition?
Despite competition from other all-rounders like Cameron Green and Beau Webster, Marsh’s skill set is still valued by selectors. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rivalry [प्रतिद्वंद्विता] is the closest meaning. Marsh faces competition from other all-rounders for a place in the team, i.e. a rivalry between players for the same spot.

Option meanings
Rivalry — competition between people for the same thing [प्रतिद्वंद्विता]
Contest — a single event in which people compete [प्रतियोगिता, मुकाबला]
Opposition — resistance or disagreement [विरोध]
Challenge — a difficult task or a call to compete [चुनौती]

question.en:
Choose the option that best describes the meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence:
The king was a benevolent ruler who ruled the kingdom for two decades. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Benevolent [परोपकारी, दयालु] means kind and generous, wishing to do good to others. So the best meaning is generous.

Option meanings
Wicked — evil, cruel [दुष्ट]
Generous — giving freely, kind [उदार]
Uncharitable — unkind, harsh [अनुदार, कठोर]
Capable — having ability [सक्षम]

Related words: Benevolent: kind, charitable, magnanimous.

question.en:
Choose the option that best describes the meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence:
Many homes were destroyed in the deluge. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Deluge [बाढ़, जलप्रलय] means a severe flood or a very heavy downpour. So the meaning is a flood of water.

Option meanings
An earthquake — shaking of the ground [भूकंप]
A drizzle — very light rain [फुहार]
A strike of lightning — flash of electricity from clouds [बिजली गिरना]
A flood of water — overflow of water on land [बाढ़]

Related words: Deluge: inundation, torrent, downpour.

question.en:
Choose the option which is similar in meaning to the underlined word.
During the ten years that he worked he accumulated a fortune. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Accumulated [संचित किया, जमा किया] means gathered or collected over a period of time. Its synonym is amassed.

Option meanings
Amassed — collected in large quantity [इकट्ठा किया]
Consumed — used up [उपभोग किया]
Dispersed — scattered [बिखेर दिया]
Distributed — shared out [बाँट दिया]

Related words: Accumulate: gather, hoard, stockpile.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word:
VENERATE [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Venerate [श्रद्धा रखना, पूजना] means to regard with great respect. Its synonym is revere.

Option meanings
Disdain — to look down upon [तिरस्कार करना]
Revere — to respect deeply [आदर करना, श्रद्धा रखना]
Ignore — to pay no attention to [अनदेखा करना]
Mock — to make fun of [उपहास करना]

Related words: Venerate: worship, honour, esteem.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word:
REMONSTRATE [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Remonstrate [विरोध प्रकट करना] means to make a forceful protest or objection. Its synonym is protest.

Option meanings
Celebrate — to mark a happy occasion [उत्सव मनाना]
Protest — to express objection [विरोध करना]
Rejoice — to feel great joy [आनंदित होना]
Surrender — to give up [आत्मसमर्पण करना]

Related words: Remonstrate: object, complain, expostulate.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word:
HAUGHTY [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Haughty [घमंडी, अभिमानी] means arrogantly superior and looking down on others. Its synonym is proud.

Option meanings
Proud — having too high an opinion of oneself [अभिमानी]
Meek — quiet and submissive [दब्बू, विनम्र]
Deferential — showing respect to others [आदरपूर्ण]
Bashful — shy [शर्मीला]

Meek, deferential and bashful are nearly opposite to haughty.

Related words: Haughty: arrogant, conceited, supercilious.

question.en:
Choose the option which is similar in meaning to the underlined word.
He did his work reluctantly because he did not like the director. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Reluctantly [अनिच्छा से] means doing something unwillingly, without interest. Work done reluctantly is done perfunctorily — just as a formality, with minimum effort.

Option meanings
Voluntarily — by one's own free will [स्वेच्छा से]
Perfunctorily — carelessly, only as a routine duty [बेमन से, औपचारिकतावश]
Enthusiastically — with great eagerness [उत्साहपूर्वक]
Thankfully — gratefully [कृतज्ञतापूर्वक]

Related words: Reluctantly: unwillingly, grudgingly, half-heartedly.

question.en:
Choose a word that is similar in meaning to the word in bold.
The young journalist jeopardized her career to save the lives of many slum children. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Jeopardized [ख़तरे में डाला] means put someone or something at risk of harm or loss. She put her career at risk, i.e. she endangered it.

Option meanings
Safeguarded — protected [सुरक्षित रखा]
Rejuvenated — made fresh or young again [नवजीवन दिया]
Endangered — put in danger [संकट में डाला]
Celebrated — honoured publicly [उत्सव मनाया/सम्मानित किया]

Related words: Jeopardize: imperil, risk, threaten.

question.en:
Choose a word that is similar in meaning to the word in bold.
Although Mona has a slight speech impediment, she still speaks confidently in front of people. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Impediment [बाधा, दोष] means a hindrance; a speech impediment is a defect in speaking, such as a stammer.

Option meanings
Advancement — progress [प्रगति]
Defect — a fault or shortcoming [दोष, कमी]
Imposition — forcing something on someone [थोपना]
Advantage — a benefit [लाभ]

Related words: Impediment: obstacle, handicap, hindrance.

question.en:
Which word can best replace highlighted?
Bailey highlighted Marsh's impressive performance against England and his ability to turn a game around. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Highlighted [ज़ोर दिया, प्रमुखता से बताया] means drew special attention to something. The best replacement is emphasized.

Option meanings
Emphasized — gave special importance to [ज़ोर दिया]
Mentioned — referred to briefly [उल्लेख किया]
Displayed — showed openly [प्रदर्शित किया]
Stressed — insisted on the importance of [बल दिया]

"Mentioned" is too weak, "displayed" does not fit, and "stressed" suggests insisting; "emphasized" best matches praising a performance.

Related words: Highlight: underline, spotlight, feature.

question.en:
Which word is closest in meaning to inclusion?
Kohli's inclusion would give India more balance and depth in the squad. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Inclusion [शामिल करना] means the act of adding someone to a group. Here it means Kohli's addition to the squad.

Option meanings
Addition — adding someone or something [जोड़ना, सम्मिलन]
Entry — the act of entering [प्रवेश]
Involvement — taking part [भागीदारी]
Presence — being present [उपस्थिति]

Related words: Inclusion: incorporation, induction, admission.

question.en:
Which word is closest in meaning to intrigued?
The discovery of a hidden void within the Great Pyramid has intrigued archaeologists worldwide. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Intrigued [जिज्ञासा जगाई] means aroused great curiosity or interest. The closest meaning is fascinated.

Option meanings
Confused — puzzled [उलझन में]
Annoyed — irritated [नाराज़]
Bored — uninterested [ऊबा हुआ]
Fascinated — strongly attracted and interested [मोहित]

Related words: Intrigue: captivate, interest, enthral.

question.en:
Choose the word which is most nearly the same in meaning to the underlined word.
The students who graduated from that school are adept at playing musical instruments. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Adept [निपुण, कुशल] means very skilled at something. The students are proficient at playing musical instruments.

Option meanings
proficient — highly skilled [प्रवीण, दक्ष]
comfortable — at ease [सहज]
careful — cautious [सावधान]
proverbial — well known, as if from a proverb [कहावती, प्रसिद्ध]

Related words: Adept: skilful, expert, accomplished.

question.en:
Choose the word which is most nearly the same in meaning to the underlined word.
Racial segregation was a reality in many countries. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Segregation [पृथक्करण, अलगाव] means keeping groups apart, especially by race. Racial segregation is racial separation.

Option meanings
integration — bringing groups together [एकीकरण]
education — teaching and learning [शिक्षा]
separation — keeping apart [अलगाव]
desertion — abandoning a person or duty [परित्याग]

Integration is the opposite of segregation.

Related words: Segregation: isolation, partition, discrimination.

question.en: What is the synonym of "Apathy"? [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Apathy [उदासीनता] means lack of interest, feeling or concern. Its synonym is indifference.

Option meanings
Interest — curiosity or attention [रुचि]
Concern — worry or care [चिंता, परवाह]
Indifference — lack of interest or concern [उदासीनता]
Compassion — sympathy for others' suffering [करुणा]

Interest, concern and compassion are nearly opposite to apathy.

Related words: Apathy: unconcern, listlessness, lethargy.

question.en:
Which word is closest in meaning to innocent?
The astrologer was as much a stranger to the stars as were his innocent customers. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The astrologer's innocent customers are easily fooled by him, i.e. they are gullible [आसानी से ठगे जाने वाले]. (From R.K. Narayan's "An Astrologer's Day".)

Option meanings
Naive — inexperienced, simple [भोला, अनुभवहीन]
Gullible — easily deceived [जल्दी ठगा जाने वाला]
Wise — having good judgement [बुद्धिमान]
Guilty — responsible for wrongdoing [दोषी]

Naive is close, but "gullible" exactly conveys being easily taken in, as the customers are.

Related words: Gullible: credulous, trusting, unsuspecting.

question.en:
Which word is nearest in meaning to stealthily?
He had left his village stealthily, without informing anyone. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Stealthily [चुपके से] means secretly, so as not to be noticed; "without informing anyone" confirms the meaning secretly.

Option meanings
Loudly — with much noise [ज़ोर से]
Boldly — bravely [साहसपूर्वक]
Secretly — without others knowing [गुप्त रूप से]
Publicly — openly [सार्वजनिक रूप से]

Related words: Stealthily: furtively, covertly, surreptitiously.

question.en:
Which word is closest in meaning to extraordinary?
A most extraordinary man, but very quiet. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Extraordinary [असाधारण] means very unusual or remarkable. Its synonym is unusual.

Option meanings
Common — ordinary [सामान्य]
Unusual — not ordinary [असामान्य]
Regular — normal, habitual [नियमित]
Average — typical [औसत]

Related words: Extraordinary: remarkable, exceptional, phenomenal.

question.en:
Which word can best replace exquisite?
The niece had an exquisite sense of drama in her storytelling. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Exquisite [उत्कृष्ट, परिष्कृत] means extremely fine and delicate. An exquisite sense of drama is a refined one.

Option meanings
Refined — elegant, polished [परिष्कृत]
Harsh — rough, severe [कठोर]
Coarse — rough, crude [भद्दा, खुरदरा]
Bland — dull, tasteless [फीका, नीरस]

Related words: Exquisite: delicate, elegant, fine.

question.en:
Choose the word which is most nearly the same in meaning to the underlined word.
Most entrepreneurs squander their profits on expensive purchases. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Squander [अपव्यय करना, गँवाना] means to waste money, time, or opportunity in a reckless, extravagant, or foolish manner. Spend wastefully is the exact synonym.

Option meanings
• use economically — to spend frugally and prudently [किफायत से खर्च करना]
• spend wastefully — to dissipate money extravagantly without prudence [फिजूलखर्ची करना]
• utilize judiciously — to use wisely with sound judgment [विवेकपूर्ण उपयोग करना]
• donate generously — to give charitably in large amounts [उदारतापूर्वक दान देना]

Related words: Squander: dissipate, fritter away, lavish, misspend.

question.en: What is the synonym of "Cacophony"? [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Cacophony [कर्कश ध्वनि, कोलाहल] (derived from the Greek kakos 'bad' + phone 'voice/sound') refers to a harsh, discordant, jarring mixture of sounds. Noise is the closest synonym among the choices.

Option meanings
• Harmony — a pleasing arrangement or concord of sounds (antonym) [तालमेल, सामंजस्य]
• Silence — complete absence of sound [शांति, मौन]
• Noise — loud, harsh, or clamorous sound [शोर, कोलाहल]
• Quiet — calm, peaceful, free from noise [शांत]

Related words: Cacophony: clamor, dissonance, din, discord, racket.

question.en: What is the synonym of "Vigorous"? [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Vigorous [ऊर्जावान, बलवान, जोरदार] is an adjective describing someone or something characterized by great physical strength, robust energy, or forceful effort. Strong is the most appropriate synonym.

Option meanings
• Weakness — lack of physical strength or resolve; a noun [कमजोरी]
• Lethargic — sluggish, drowsy, devoid of energy (antonym) [सुस्त, शिथिल]
• Strong — possessing physical power, robustness, or resilience [बलवान, मजबूत]
• Fragile — easily broken, delicate (antonym) [नाजुक, भंगुर]

Related words: Vigorous: robust, energetic, forceful, dynamic, sturdy.

question.en:
Which word is closest in meaning to brusque?
His demeanor was brusque, but not unkind. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Brusque [रूखा, अशिष्ट, अचानक] describes behavior or speech that is blunt, abrupt, and curt in manner, often to the point of seeming rude. Abrupt is the exact synonym.

Option meanings
• Gentle — mild and kind (antonym) [विनम्र, कोमल]
• Calm — serene and peaceful [शांत]
• Abrupt — sudden, curt, blunt, and brief [रूखा, एकाएक]
• Polite — courteous and respectful (antonym) [शिष्ट]

Related words: Brusque: curt, terse, blunt, snappish, gruff.

question.en:
Which word is closest in meaning to haphazard?
The place was lit up with haphazard lights and smoky lanterns. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Haphazard [बेतरतीब, अस्त-व्यस्त, आकस्मिक] means lacking any obvious principle of organization, order, or regular plan. Random is the exact synonym.

Option meanings
• Planned — arranged in advance (antonym) [योजनाबद्ध]
• Random — made, done, or happening without method or conscious choice [यादृच्छिक, बेतरतीब]
• Fixed — predetermined, stable [स्थिर]
• Uniform — remaining the same in all cases, consistent [एकसमान]

Related words: Haphazard: chaotic, unmethodical, disorderly, erratic.

question.en:
Which word is nearest in meaning to robust?
His nerves were far from robust. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Robust [मजबूत, पुष्ट, शक्तिशाली] describes a person or system that is strong, sturdy, healthy, and vigorous. In the context of nerves or constitution, not robust means frail. Hence, Strong is the exact synonym.

Option meanings
• Strong — having great physical power or stamina [मजबूत]
• Weak — lacking strength (antonym) [कमजोर]
• Nervous — anxious or apprehensive [चिंतित, घबराया हुआ]
• Fragile — delicate, easily damaged (antonym) [नाजुक]

Related words: Robust: vigorous, sturdy, resilient, hardy, stalwart.

question.en:
Which word is nearest in meaning to withstood?
The pyramids have withstood the ravages of time, remaining largely intact for millennia. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Withstand (past tense: withstood) [सामना करना, झेल जाना, टिके रहना] means to resist successfully, hold out against, or survive hostile forces, wear, or damage. Endured is the exact synonym.

Option meanings
• Collapsed — broke down, crumbled (antonym) [ढह गया]
• Endured — survived, lasted, remained intact through adversity [सहन किया, टिका रहा]
• Avoided — kept away from [बचा]
• Surrendered — yielded or gave up (antonym) [समर्पण कर दिया]

Related words: Withstood: tolerated, braved, outlasted, weathered.

question.en: What is the synonym of "Ravenous"? [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Meaning: Ravenous = extremely hungry; having a great desire for food.
Synonym: Hungry.

Why other options are wrong
Satisfied and Full are antonyms; Thirsty refers to a need for drink, not food.

Therefore, Hungry.

question.en:
Which word means the same as choose?
England is set to choose their squad for the World Test Championship final against South Africa. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Meaning: Choose = to pick out from a number of options.
For a sports squad, the standard word is to select the team – “England is set to select their squad …”.

Other options
Elect is used for voting (elect a leader); Nominate is to propose someone for a post or award; Pick is informal and close, but “select” is the precise formal equivalent used for squads.

Therefore, Select.

question.en:
Which word can best replace comprehension?
Framton shivered slightly and turned towards the niece with a look intended to convey sympathetic comprehension. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Meaning: Comprehension = the ability to understand.
“Sympathetic comprehension” = sympathetic understanding.
Confusion and Doubt are opposites; Question is unrelated.

Therefore, Understanding.

question.en: The region has abundant natural resources, making it economically strong. Choose the word that is closest synonym to "ABUNDANT". [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Meaning: Abundant = existing in large quantities; more than enough.
Synonym: Plentiful.
Scarce, Rare and Limited are antonyms.

Therefore, Plentiful.

question.en: The committee rejected the proposal because it was considered ambiguous and open to multiple interpretations. The lack of clarity caused confusion among members and prevented them from reaching a clear decision. Which word is closest synonym to ambiguous? [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Meaning: Ambiguous = open to more than one interpretation; not clear. The passage itself explains it: “open to multiple interpretations … lack of clarity”.
Synonym: Vague.
Clear, Definite and Precise are antonyms.

Therefore, Vague.

question.en: The leader was known for his pragmatic approach to solving problems. He focused on practical solutions rather than ideal theories, making decisions based on real-world conditions and achievable results. Which word is closest synonym to pragmatic? [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Meaning: Pragmatic = dealing with things sensibly and realistically. The passage explains it: “practical solutions rather than ideal theories”.
Synonym: Practical.
Idealistic and Theoretical are opposites; Emotional is unrelated.

Therefore, Practical.

question.en: Select the synonym of Eager. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** **Eager** means strongly wanting to do or have something, characterized by keen interest or enthusiasm.
**Synonym:** **Enthusiastic** means showing intense and eager enjoyment, interest, or approval.
**Other options:** **Lazy** and **idle** mean unwilling to work or inactive; **dull** means lacking interest or brightness.

question.en: Select the synonym of Genuine. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** **Genuine** means truly what something is said to be; authentic and real.
**Synonym:** **Real** means actually existing or being what it appears or is claimed to be.
**Other options:** **False**, **fake**, and **counterfeit** are direct antonyms signifying non-authentic or fraudulent items.

question.en: Select the synonym of Nimble. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** **Nimble** means quick and light in movement or action; agile.
**Synonym:** **Quick** refers to moving or capable of moving with high speed.
**Other options:** **Clumsy** and **slow** are direct antonyms of nimble; **careless** means not giving sufficient attention or thought.

question.en: Select the synonym of Revoke. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** **Revoke** means to officially cancel, repeal, or annul a decree, decision, or promise.
**Synonym:** **Cancel** means to decide that an agreed-upon event or valid status will not happen or be legally in effect.
**Other options:** **Improve** means to make better; **permit** means to allow; **confirm** means to validate or establish firmly.

question.en: Select the synonym of Tranquil. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** **Tranquil** means free from disturbance, calm, and serene.
**Synonym:** **Peaceful** means free from disturbance or agitation.
**Other options:** **Agitated** and **violent** are antonyms denoting commotion or extreme disturbance; **sad** denotes feeling sorrow.

question.en: Select the synonym of Abolish. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** **Abolish** means to formally put an end to a system, practice, or institution.
**Synonym:** **Eliminate** means to completely remove or get rid of something.
**Other options:** **Establish**, **construct**, and **approve** are antonyms that describe building, enacting, or accepting something.

question.en: Select the synonym of Brief. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Brief [संक्षिप्त] means short in duration or length. Short is the closest meaning.

Option meanings
Short — lasting little time [संक्षिप्त]
Long — of great length [लंबा]
Wide — of great width [चौड़ा]
Deep — of great depth [गहरा]

Related words: Brief: concise, succinct, terse.

question.en: Select the synonym of Marvel. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Marvel [अद्भुतता, आश्चर्य] means a feeling of wonder or something astonishing. Wonder is the closest.

Option meanings
Wonder — amazement [आश्चर्य]
Horror — intense fear [खौफ]
Fear — being afraid [डर]
Shame — disgrace [शर्म]

Related words: Marvel: miracle, phenomenon, prodigy.

question.en: Select the synonym of Plausible. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Plausible [विश्वसनीय लगने वाला] means seeming reasonable or believable. Credible is the closest synonym.

Option meanings
Unlikely — not probable [असंभावित]
Credible — believable [विश्वसनीय]
Weak — lacking strength [कमज़ोर]
Impossible — not possible [असंभव]

Related words: Plausible: reasonable, convincing, probable.

question.en: Select the synonym of Reside. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Reside [निवास करना] means to live in a place. Dwell is the closest synonym.

Option meanings
Depart — leave [रवाना होना]
Dwell — live [निवास करना]
Move — change position [हिलना]
Resign — quit a job [इस्तीफा देना]

Related words: Reside: inhabit, occupy, abide.

question.en: Select the synonym of Ostentatious. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Ostentatious [दिखावटी] means showy, designed to attract attention. Showy is the closest synonym.

Option meanings
Modest — humble [विनम्र]
Showy — flashy [दिखावटी]
Humble — unpretentious [साधारण]
Quiet — silent [शांत]

Related words: Ostentatious: flashy, pretentious, flamboyant.

question.en:
Select the most approptiate synonym of the word:
RECALCITRANT [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Recalcitrant [अवज्ञाकारी] means stubbornly resistant to authority or control. Unruly is the closest synonym.

Option meanings
Obedient — compliant [आज्ञाकारी]
Unruly — disorderly, defiant [अवश्य]
Compliant — yielding [अनुवर्ती]
Respectful — courteous [सम्मानजनक]

Related words: Recalcitrant: defiant, stubborn, refractory.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
The peace treaty received broad acceptance from all the nations involved. [Selection Post (Graduate) 17 Sep 2026 Shift 1]
question.hi:

Refusal means denial; Delay means postponement; Confusion means lack of clarity.

• Consensus: General agreement among a group (आम सहमति)
• Refusal: The act of saying no (इनकार)
• Delay: A period of waiting; lateness (विलंब / देरी)
• Confusion: Lack of understanding (भ्रम / उलझन)

• Certain: Sure; definite (निश्चित)
• Approaching: Coming nearer (निकट आता हुआ)

question.en: Choose the word that means the same as "Enormous". [Selection Post (Graduate) 18 Sep 2026 Shift 1]
question.hi: Choose the word that means the same as "Enormous". [Selection Post (Graduate) 18 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

Regular exercise may obviate the need for certain medications later in life. [Selection Post (Graduate) 19 Sep 2026 Shift 1]
question.hi:
Choose the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
Regular exercise may obviate the need for certain medications later in life. [Selection Post (Graduate) 19 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Meaning: Obviate means to remove a need or difficulty, or to prevent something from happening.
Synonym: Prevent correctly conveys the meaning of avoiding or making unnecessary.
Other options: Delay means to postpone; Complicate means to make difficult; Replace means to take the place of.
Vocab Meanings:
• Obviate: To remove a need or prevent a problem (टालना / अनावश्यक बना देना)
• Delay: To make late; to postpone (विलंब करना)
• Prevent: To stop something happening (रोकना)
• Complicate: To make more difficult (जटिल बनाना)
• Replace: To take the place of (प्रतिस्थापित करना)

Choose the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
The querulous customer argued about everything. [Selection Post (Graduate) 19 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

question.en: Choose the word that means the same as "Reproduce". [Selection Post (Graduate) 21 Sep 2026 Shift 1]
question.hi: Choose the word that means the same as "Reproduce". [Selection Post (Graduate) 21 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:

Other options:
• Stipulate: Demand or specify a requirement as part of an agreement.
• Progression: The process of developing or moving gradually towards a more advanced state.
• Prohibit: Formally forbid something by law, rule, or authority.
Vocab Meanings:
• Reproduce: To produce offspring or copies (प्रजनन करना / पुनः उत्पन्न करना)
• Proliferate: To increase rapidly in number (तेज़ी से बढ़ना / प्रजनन करना)
• Stipulate: To state as a condition (शर्त रखना / निर्धारित करना)
• Progression: The process of moving forward (प्रगति / क्रम)
• Prohibit: To forbid by law (निषेध करना)

• Submissive: Willing to obey others (विनम्र / अधीन)
• Cooperative: Willing to work together (सहयोगी)

question.en: In the Indian census, "resident" is the opposite of: [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
In census enumeration, a resident [निवासी] is a person who normally lives in the household or place. Its opposite is a visitor, who is present only temporarily.

Option meanings
Visitor — a person staying only for a short time [आगंतुक]
Landlord — a person who lets out property [मकान-मालिक]
Tenant — a person who rents property; a tenant can still be a resident [किरायेदार]
Citizen — a legal member of a nation [नागरिक]

Related words: Resident: inhabitant, occupant, dweller.

Option meanings
Authentic — genuine; of undisputed origin [प्रामाणिक, असली]
FALSE — not true [असत्य]
Fake — not genuine [नकली]
Fraudulent — obtained or done by deception [कपटपूर्ण]

Related words: Apocryphal: spurious, fictitious, unverified.

question.en:

solution.en:
Abnegation [आत्म-त्याग, आत्म-संयम] means renouncing one’s own desires or comforts. Its antonym is indulgence, allowing oneself pleasures freely.

Option meanings
Indulgence — allowing oneself whatever one enjoys [भोग-विलास, लिप्तता]
Moderation — avoiding excess [संयम]
Compassion — sympathy for others’ suffering [करुणा]
Contentment — satisfaction [संतोष]

Related words: Abnegation: self-denial, renunciation, abstinence.

question.en: What is the antonym of "Superfluous"? [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Superfluous [अनावश्यक, फ़ालतू] means more than what is needed. Its antonym is essential.

Option meanings
Excessive — more than necessary [अत्यधिक]
Essential — absolutely necessary [अनिवार्य, आवश्यक]
Unnecessary — not needed [अनावश्यक]
Extravagant — spending or using too much [फ़िज़ूलखर्च]

Related words: Superfluous: redundant, surplus, needless.

question.en: What is the antonym of "Egregious"? [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

Egregious [घोर, अत्यंत बुरा] means outstandingly bad or shocking, as in “an egregious error”. Its antonym is minor — small and unimportant.

Option meanings
Blatant — done openly and obviously [स्पष्ट, खुल्लमखुल्ला]
Horrific — causing horror [भयावह]
Minor — small in size or importance [मामूली]
Appalling — shockingly bad [भयानक]

Related words: Egregious: flagrant, glaring, outrageous.

isolated — separated from others [अलग-थलग]

question.en: Choose the antonym of 'detain': [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

question.en: What is the antonym of "Enervate"? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

Exhaust — to tire out completely [थका देना]

question.en: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Contrite [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

Contrite [पश्चातापी] means feeling sorry and guilty for having done wrong.

question.en: What is the antonym of "Sycophantic"? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

Sycophantic [चापलूसी करने वाला] means trying to win favour by flattering powerful people.

question.en: What is the antonym of "Dilatory"? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Dilatory [विलंबकारी] means slow and tending to cause delay.

Prompt — quick, without delay [तत्पर, शीघ्र]

question.en: What is the antonym of "Magnanimous"? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

Magnanimous [उदार, महामना] means generous and forgiving, especially towards a rival or someone less powerful.
Its antonym is Selfish, meaning caring only about oneself.

Option meanings
Selfish — concerned only with oneself [स्वार्थी]
Charitable — kind and generous to those in need [दानशील] (synonym)
Noble — having high moral qualities [महान] (synonym)
Generous — willing to give freely [उदार] (synonym)

question.en: What is the antonym of "Opprobrium"? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

Opprobrium [घोर निंदा, अपयश] means harsh public criticism or the disgrace it brings.

Option meanings
Infamy — the state of being well known for something bad [कुख्याति] (synonym)
Dishonor — loss of respect [अपमान] (synonym)
Honor — great respect [सम्मान]
Shame — disgrace [लज्जा] (synonym)

question.en:
Choose the correct antonym of the word:

Stubborn — unwilling to change [जिद्दी]

Related words: Antonyms of obstinate: compliant, flexible, amenable.

question.en:
Choose the correct antonym of the word:
FERVENT [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

Fervent [उत्कट, जोशीला] means showing intense feeling or enthusiasm. Its antonym is indifferent.

Indifferent — showing no interest [उदासीन]
Passionate — full of strong feeling [उत्साही, भावुक]

Related words: Antonyms of fervent: apathetic, lukewarm, unenthusiastic.

question.en:
Choose the correct antonym of the word:
GULLIBLE. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

Gullible [आसानी से ठगा जाने वाला] means easily deceived because of trusting too readily. Its antonym is skeptical.

Naive — lacking experience, simple [भोला]

Related words: Antonyms of gullible: suspicious, wary, distrustful.

question.en: What is the antonym of "Loquacious"? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Loquacious [बातूनी] means very talkative. Its antonym is reticent.

Option meanings
Talkative — fond of talking [बातूनी]

question.en: What is the antonym of "Mellifluous"? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

Mellifluous [मधुर, कर्णप्रिय] means sweet and pleasant to hear. Its antonym is harsh.

Melodious — tuneful [सुरीला]

Related words: Antonyms of mellifluous: grating, strident, discordant.

question.en: What is the antonym of "Labyrinthine"? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

Labyrinthine [भूलभुलैया जैसा, जटिल] means like a maze — winding and complicated. Its antonym is linear.

Winding — full of turns [घुमावदार]

Winding, meandering and serpentine are close in meaning to labyrinthine.

Related words: Antonyms of labyrinthine: straight, simple, direct.

question.en:
Choose the word which conveys the OPPOSITE meaning for the word "Feisty"

Feisty [जोशीला, साहसी] means lively, spirited and ready to fight. Its opposite is cowardly.

sorrow — sadness [दुःख]
dauntless — fearless [निडर]
plucky — brave [हिम्मती]
cowardly — lacking courage [कायरतापूर्ण]

Dauntless and plucky are synonyms of feisty, and sorrow is unrelated.

question.en:
Choose the word which has the opposite meaning to the given word:

Lassitude [थकान, सुस्ती] means physical or mental tiredness and lack of energy. Its opposite is enthusiasm.

question.en: What is the antonym of "Impecunious"? [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

question.en: What is the antonym of "Ebullient"? [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

Ebullient [उत्साह से भरपूर, प्रफुल्लित] means cheerful and full of energy. Its opposite is depressed.

question.en: What is the antonym of "Sybaritic"? [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

question.en: What is the antonym of "Acerbic"? [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

question.en:
Choose the word which conveys the OPPOSITE meaning for the word "OUTLANDISH"
The manager said, "All ideas, no matter how outlandish, will be considered". [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Outlandish [विचित्र, अस्वाभाविक, बेतुका] means looking, sounding, or seeming bizarre, unconventional, or wildly improbable. In the context of creative proposals, ideas that are outlandish are far-fetched and improbable. The antonym is plausible (reasonable, believable, and practically feasible).

• Quirky — having peculiar or unexpected traits [अजीब, अनोखा]
• Atypical — not representative of a type, unusual [अप्राकृतिक, असामान्य]
• plausible — seeming reasonable, credible, or probable (antonym) [विश्वसनीय, तर्कसंगत]
• Crotchety — irritable, eccentric, bad-tempered [चिड़चिड़ा]

Related words: Outlandish: bizarre, preposterous, grotesque, eccentric.

question.en: What is the antonym of "Acrimonious"? [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

question.en: What is the antonym of "Tangible"? [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

question.en:

Therefore, obnoxious.

solution.en:

• Eclipse: An obscuring of the light from one celestial body by the passage of another between it and the observer.

• Zenith: The highest point (शिखर / चरम बिंदु)
• Eclipse: The blocking of light of one heavenly body by another (ग्रहण)

question.en: What is the name of a procedure where a piece of tissue or a sample of cells from the body is removed so that a medical pathologist can examine it? [Selection Post (12th) 17 Sep 2026 Shift 2]
question.hi: What is the name of a procedure where a piece of tissue or a sample of cells from the body is removed so that a medical pathologist can examine it? [Selection Post (12th) 17 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Biopsy is the surgical removal of a small sample of living tissue or cells for diagnostic pathological examination.
Other options: An autopsy is a post-mortem examination performed after death; an operation is a generic term for any surgical intervention; an amputation is the surgical severance of a body limb.
Vocab Meanings:
• Biopsy: Removal of tissue from a living body for medical examination (ऊतक परीक्षण / बायोप्सी)
• Autopsy: Examination of a dead body to find the cause of death (शव परीक्षा / पोस्टमार्टम)
• Operation: A surgical procedure (शल्य क्रिया)
• Amputation: Cutting off a body part by surgery (अंग विच्छेदन)

question.en: What does the idiom 'Hobson's choice' mean? [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Hobson’s choice [मजबूरी का एकमात्र विकल्प] is a situation in which only one option is offered: take it or leave it.

Option meanings
A free option — a choice made freely [स्वतंत्र विकल्प]
No real choice at all — only one thing is available [कोई वास्तविक विकल्प नहीं]
Two equal options — alternatives of equal value [दो बराबर विकल्प]
A sudden decision — a decision made quickly [अचानक लिया गया निर्णय]

The phrase comes from Thomas Hobson, a Cambridge stable-keeper who made customers take the horse nearest the door or none.

Related words: Contextual equivalents: take it or leave it, no alternative.

2.en: To decline in condition or quality

solution.en:
To go to the dogs [बर्बाद हो जाना, बदहाल होना] means to decline badly in condition or quality.

Option meanings
To be successful — to achieve success [सफल होना]
To decline in condition or quality — to get worse [बदतर होना]
To get along well — to have a good relationship [अच्छा तालमेल होना]
To become an animal lover — literal and unrelated [पशु-प्रेमी बनना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: deteriorate, go downhill, go to rack and ruin.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To have too many irons in the fire [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

2.en: To be involved in too many activities at once

solution.en:
To have too many irons in the fire [एक साथ बहुत सारे कामों में उलझे रहना] means to be involved in too many activities at the same time.

Option meanings
To be very focused — concentrating on one thing [पूरी तरह एकाग्र होना]
To be involved in too many activities at once — taking on too much [एक साथ बहुत से कामों में लगे रहना]
To be lazy — unwilling to work [आलसी होना]
To be a blacksmith — literal and unrelated [लोहार होना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: spread oneself too thin, overcommit.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To flog a dead horse [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: To revive interest in a subject

2.en: To waste effort on a lost cause

solution.en:
To flog a dead horse [व्यर्थ प्रयास करना] means to waste effort on something that is already finished or hopeless.

Option meanings
To revive interest in a subject — to renew attention [रुचि फिर जगाना]
To waste effort on a lost cause — to keep trying uselessly [निरर्थक प्रयास करना]
To beat an animal — literal and unrelated [पशु को पीटना]
To work very hard — to put in great effort [कड़ी मेहनत करना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: beat a dead horse, labour in vain, waste one’s breath.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To hit the nail on the head [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
To hit the nail on the head [बिल्कुल सही बात कहना] means to be exactly right — to describe a situation or problem very accurately.

Option meanings
To miss the point — to fail to understand the main idea [मुख्य बात न समझना]
To guess correctly — to make a lucky right guess [सही अनुमान लगाना]
To be very accurate — to be exactly right [बिल्कुल सटीक होना]
To strike something hard — literal hitting [ज़ोर से मारना]

The idiom is about precision, not a lucky guess.

Related words: Contextual equivalents: be spot on, be precise, get it exactly right.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To turn over a new leaf [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

2.en: To change one's behavior for the better

solution.en:
To turn over a new leaf [नई शुरुआत करना, सुधर जाना] means to change one’s behaviour for the better.

Option meanings
To start reading a book — literal [किताब पढ़ना शुरू करना]
To change one's behavior for the better — to reform oneself [अपना आचरण सुधारना]
To keep turning pages — literal [पन्ने पलटते रहना]
To return to bad habits — to relapse [पुरानी बुरी आदतों पर लौटना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: reform, make a fresh start, mend one’s ways.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To throw in the towel [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
To throw in the towel [हार मान लेना] means to surrender or admit defeat. It comes from boxing, where a trainer throws a towel into the ring to concede.

Option meanings
To surrender or admit defeat — to give up [हार मानना]
To clean up — to tidy [साफ़ करना]
To continue fighting — to keep going [लड़ते रहना]
To start a new task — to begin something new [नया काम शुरू करना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: give up, concede, call it quits.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
A bad workman always blames his tools [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

1.en: To blame external factors for poor performance

2.en: To fix equipment before starting work

3.en: To hire assistants when a task is difficult to complete

4.en: To refuse to work without proper training

solution.en:
The proverb A bad workman always blames his tools [नाच न जाने आँगन टेढ़ा] means that people who perform poorly blame outside factors instead of their own lack of skill.

Option meanings
To blame external factors for poor performance — shifting the blame [दोष दूसरों पर डालना]
To fix equipment before starting work — preparing tools [काम से पहले औज़ार ठीक करना]
To hire assistants when a task is difficult to complete — seeking help [सहायक रखना]
To refuse to work without proper training — insisting on training [प्रशिक्षण के बिना काम न करना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: make excuses, pass the buck.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Hit the nail on the head [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

1.en: To identify the exact point or truth

2.en: To perform a difficult task with ease

3.en: To be precise in a dangerous situation

4.en: To strike a heavy object forcefully

solution.en:
Hit the nail on the head [बिल्कुल सही बात कहना] means to identify the exact point or truth of a matter.

Option meanings
To identify the exact point or truth — to be exactly right [सटीक बात पकड़ना]
To perform a difficult task with ease — to do something effortlessly [कठिन काम आसानी से करना]
To be precise in a dangerous situation — to act accurately in danger [खतरे में सटीक रहना]
To strike a heavy object forcefully — literal hitting [ज़ोर से प्रहार करना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: be spot on, put one’s finger on it.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Read somebody the Riot Act [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

1.en: To explain a rule in great detail

2.en: To participate in a public protest

3.en: To read aloud from a law textbook

solution.en:
To read somebody the Riot Act [कड़ी फटकार लगाना] means to reprimand someone very severely and warn them to stop behaving badly.

Option meanings
To explain a rule in great detail — a detailed explanation [नियम विस्तार से समझाना]
To participate in a public protest — joining a demonstration [सार्वजनिक विरोध में भाग लेना]
To read aloud from a law textbook — literal reading [कानून की किताब पढ़ना]
To reprimand someone very severely — to scold sternly [कड़ी फटकार लगाना]

The phrase comes from the British Riot Act of 1714, which was read aloud to order unruly crowds to disperse.

Related words: Contextual equivalents: give a dressing-down, haul over the coals, rebuke.

question.en:
In the following question, four alternatives are given for the Idiom/Phrase underlined in the sentence. Choose the option that best expresses its meaning.
The politician's sudden apology was clearly a face-saving measure. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Face-saving [अपनी साख या इज़्ज़त बचाने वाला] describes an action meant to avoid embarrassment or protect one's reputation.
The politician apologised suddenly to limit damage to his image, not out of sincerity.

Example: The minister's resignation was seen as a face-saving move after the scandal.

question.en:
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom:
Go the extra mile [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Go the extra mile [अतिरिक्त प्रयास करना] means to make more effort than is expected.

Example: Good teachers go the extra mile to help weak students.

question.en:
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom:
Throw cold water on [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Throw cold water on [हतोत्साहित करना, पानी फेरना] means to discourage an idea or plan.

Example: The manager threw cold water on our proposal for a new branch.

question.en: What does the idiom "On the ball" mean? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
On the ball [सतर्क और सक्षम] means alert, quick to understand and competent.

Example: Our new accountant is really on the ball; she spotted the error at once.

question.en: What does the phrase "Off the cuff" mean? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Off the cuff [बिना तैयारी के] means spoken or done without preparation.

Example: He made an off-the-cuff speech at the farewell party.

question.en: What is the meaning of the phrase "Hold your horses"? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Hold your horses [धैर्य रखो, रुको] means wait a moment and do not act too hastily.

Example: Hold your horses! Let us read the terms before signing.

question.en: What does the idiom "Go the extra mile" mean? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Go the extra mile [अपेक्षा से अधिक प्रयास करना] means to do more than what is necessary or expected.

Example: The nurse went the extra mile to comfort the patient's family.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
In the doldrums [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: Feeling lost in a large crowd

2.en: A state of stagnation or depression

4.en: A period of extreme hot weather

solution.en:
In the doldrums [मंदी या उदासी की स्थिति में] means in a state of stagnation, inactivity or low spirits.

Example: The real estate market has been in the doldrums for two years.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
To go the whole hog [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

1.en: To consume a very large meal quickly

2.en: To do something fully and thoroughly

3.en: To act in an extremely greedy manner

4.en: To waste all of one's personal savings

solution.en:
To go the whole hog [पूरी तरह से करना] means to do something fully and thoroughly, without holding back.

Example: Once they decided to renovate the kitchen, they went the whole hog and replaced everything.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
To chew someone out [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

1.en: To invite someone for an expensive dinner

2.en: To mock someone behind their back

3.en: To scold or reprimand someone severely

4.en: To praise someone for doing good work

solution.en:
To chew someone out [कड़ी फटकार लगाना] means to scold or reprimand someone severely.

Example: The coach chewed the players out for arriving late to practice.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Cold feet [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Cold feet [घबराहट, हिचकिचाहट] means feeling nervous or hesitant, especially just before doing something important; it is usually used as "get cold feet".

Example: He got cold feet just before his first stage performance.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Eat humble pie [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

1.en: To admit a mistake and apologise

2.en: To eat a meal that is very cheap

4.en: To be forced to eat against your will

solution.en:
Eat humble pie [अपनी गलती मानकर माफ़ी माँगना] means to admit that one was wrong and apologise, often in a humiliating situation.

Example: After his prediction proved wrong, the critic had to eat humble pie.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Feather one's nest [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

3.en: To enrich oneself using one's position

solution.en:
Feather one's nest [अपना घर भरना] means to make oneself rich, often dishonestly, by using one's position or job.

Example: The corrupt official feathered his nest with public funds.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Get wind of something [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

1.en: To experience a sudden change in the weather

2.en: To learn about a secret or private matter

3.en: To catch a severe respiratory illness

4.en: To lose one's breath after running fast

solution.en:
Get wind of something means to hear or learn about something secret or private [भनक लगना].

Example: The press got wind of the minister's resignation before it was announced.

The idiom has nothing to do with weather, illness or losing breath.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Sail close to the wind [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

1.en: To act on the verge of illegal behaviour

2.en: To travel rapidly using a sailing ship

3.en: To choose an easy path to avoid danger

4.en: To forecast weather changes with accuracy

solution.en:
Sail close to the wind means to take a risk by doing something that is almost illegal or unacceptable [कानून/नियम की सीमा पर चलना].

Example: The company sailed close to the wind with its misleading advertisements.

It comes from sailing: steering too close to the direction of the wind risks capsizing.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Cry for the moon [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

3.en: To weep during a lunar eclipse

solution.en:
Cry for the moon means to want something that is impossible to get [असंभव वस्तु की कामना करना].

Example: Expecting to become a millionaire overnight is crying for the moon.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Tied herself up in knots [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

3.en: To complete a difficult craft project

4.en: To decorate a room with ribbons

solution.en:
Tie oneself (up) in knots means to become very confused, worried or anxious [उलझन/घबराहट में पड़ जाना].

Example: She tied herself up in knots trying to explain the delay to her boss.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Want to curl up and die [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

1.en: To suffer from a severe physical illness

2.en: To feel extreme embarrassment or shame

3.en: To prefer sleeping in a small space

4.en: To give up on a difficult goal

solution.en:
Want to curl up and die means to feel extremely embarrassed or ashamed [शर्म से गड़ जाना].

Example: When he forgot his lines on stage, he wanted to curl up and die.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Bird's eye view [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

2.en: A target seen from a great distance

3.en: A small bird flying in the sky

4.en: A wide, general view from above

solution.en:
Bird's eye view means a wide, general view seen from above, or an overall view of a subject [विहंगम दृश्य].

Example: The tower offers a bird's eye view of the city.

It is the opposite of a detailed close-up inspection.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Leave it on the back burner [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

1.en: To postpone a task or project

2.en: To cook a meal at a low heat

3.en: To store items in a kitchen cupboard

4.en: To prioritise an urgent matter immediately

solution.en:
Leave/put something on the back burner means to postpone it or give it low priority [टाल देना, बाद के लिए छोड़ देना].

Example: The expansion plan has been left on the back burner until funds are available.

Option 4 gives the opposite meaning.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Leave no stone unturned [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

1.en: To build a wall around a garden

3.en: To move heavy rocks in a field

4.en: To ignore small details in a report

solution.en:
Leave no stone unturned means to search every possible place or make every possible effort [कोई कसर न छोड़ना].

Example: The police left no stone unturned in their search for the missing child.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To give the cold shoulder [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
To give the cold shoulder [अनदेखा करना, रूखा व्यवहार करना] means to ignore or slight someone deliberately.

Option meanings
To show kindness — the opposite idea [दया दिखाना]
To ignore or slight — correct [उपेक्षा करना]
To embrace warmly — to welcome [गले लगाना]
To show support — to back someone [समर्थन करना]

Example: After the argument, she gave him the cold shoulder.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To pay through the nose [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

2.en: To pay an extremely high price

solution.en:
To pay through the nose [बहुत अधिक कीमत चुकाना] means to pay a very high or unfair price.

Option meanings
To pay a fair price — opposite idea [उचित मूल्य देना]
To pay an extremely high price — correct [बहुत महँगा चुकाना]
To pay on time — punctual payment [समय पर भुगतान]
To pay slowly — delayed payment [धीरे-धीरे भुगतान]

Example: Tourists pay through the nose for water at the airport.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Through thick and thin [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: Across a varied and difficult terrain

3.en: Through a fast and sudden physical change

4.en: Under all conditions, both good and bad

solution.en:
Through thick and thin [हर परिस्थिति में] means under all conditions, both good and bad.

Option meanings
Across a varied and difficult terrain — literal, wrong
Between two very different options — wrong
Through a fast and sudden physical change — wrong
Under all conditions, both good and bad — correct [सुख-दुःख में]

Example: True friends stand by you through thick and thin.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Go against the grain [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: To act contrary to one's principles

2.en: To saw wood in the wrong direction

4.en: To define the borders of a country

solution.en:
Go against the grain [स्वभाव/सिद्धांत के विरुद्ध जाना] means to act contrary to one's principles or natural inclination.

Option meanings
To act contrary to one's principles — correct [अपने सिद्धांतों के विरुद्ध]
To saw wood in the wrong direction — literal, wrong
To be physically very strong — wrong
To define the borders of a country — wrong

Example: It goes against the grain for him to tell a lie.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Hold a candle to [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: To be a very religious person

2.en: To provide light in a dark room

3.en: To be as good as someone else

solution.en:
Hold a candle to [बराबरी करना] means to be as good as someone else; it is mostly used in the negative ("cannot hold a candle to").

Option meanings
To be a very religious person — wrong
To provide light in a dark room — literal, wrong
To be as good as someone else — correct [बराबरी का होना]
To waste time doing nothing — wrong

Example: No other singer can hold a candle to her.

question.en:
Choose the alternative which gives the correct meaning of the given idiom or phrase.
Burn the candle at both ends [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: To light two candles at once to save time

2.en: To live a life of extreme luxury and waste

3.en: To balance two different jobs successfully

4.en: To exhaust oneself by working excessively

solution.en:
Burn the candle at both ends [अत्यधिक काम करके थक जाना] means to exhaust oneself by working too hard, e.g. late at night and early in the morning.

Option meanings
To light two candles at once to save time — literal, wrong
To live a life of extreme luxury and waste — wrong
To balance two different jobs successfully — wrong
To exhaust oneself by working excessively — correct [ख़ुद को थका देना]

Example: Before exams, many students burn the candle at both ends.

question.en: What is the meaning of the phrase "Elephantine task"? [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Elephantine task [बहुत बड़ा और कठिन काम] means a huge, difficult task; "elephantine" means enormous, like an elephant.

Option meanings
A huge difficult task — correct [विशाल और कठिन कार्य]
A secret mission — wrong
A simple chore — opposite
A task involving elephants — literal, wrong

Example: Rebuilding the flooded town was an elephantine task.

question.en: What does the phrase "Pass the buck" mean? [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Pass the buck [ज़िम्मेदारी दूसरे पर टालना] means to shift responsibility or blame to someone else.

Option meanings
To bet money — wrong
To evade responsibility — correct [ज़िम्मेदारी से बचना]
To speak briefly — wrong
To transfer something — literal, wrong

Example: When the project failed, the manager tried to pass the buck to his team.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To steal a march [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
To steal a march [चुपके से बढ़त हासिल करना] means to gain an advantage over someone by acting earlier or secretly.

Option meanings
To march secretly — literal, wrong
To obtain an advantage secretly — correct [चुपके से बढ़त पाना]
To move slowly — wrong
To steal something — literal, wrong

Example: Our rival stole a march on us by launching its product a month early.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To keep a stiff upper lip [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

2.en: To remain stoic and unemotional in adversity

solution.en:
To keep a stiff upper lip [विपत्ति में धैर्य रखना] means to stay calm and not show one's feelings in difficult situations.

Option meanings
To cry easily — opposite
To remain stoic and unemotional in adversity — correct [विपत्ति में शांत और धैर्यवान रहना]
To smile broadly — wrong
To talk loudly — wrong

Example: Even after losing his job, he kept a stiff upper lip.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To hang in the balance [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
To hang in the balance [अधर में लटकना] means to be in an uncertain state, with the outcome undecided.

Option meanings
To be certain — opposite
To have an uncertain outcome — correct [परिणाम अनिश्चित होना]
To be well supported — wrong
To be easily managed — wrong

Example: The patient's life hung in the balance after the accident.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To get out of hand [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
To get out of hand [नियंत्रण से बाहर होना] means to become impossible to control.

Option meanings
To be controlled — opposite
To become uncontrollable — correct [बेक़ाबू होना]
To receive a gift — literal, wrong
To give advice — wrong

Example: The protest got out of hand, and the police had to intervene.

question.en: What does the idiom 'To weather the storm' mean? [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
To weather the storm [कठिन परिस्थिति का सफलतापूर्वक सामना करना] is an idiomatic expression that means to survive, endure, or successfully come through a difficult period, crisis, or misfortune without succumbing.

Option meanings
• Face difficulties bravely — to confront hardships with resilience and successfully endure [मुश्किलों का डटकर सामना करना]
• Hide from problems — to evade or conceal oneself from adversity [समस्याओं से छिपना]
• Avoid responsibilities — to shirk duties or obligations [दायित्वों से बचना]
• Start a new project — to embark on a fresh undertaking [नई योजना शुरू करना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: ride out, pull through, withstand, hold out.

question.en: What does the idiom "Chew the fat" mean? [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
To chew the fat [अनौपचारिक गपशप करना] is an informal idiom meaning to chat leisurely, engage in friendly, prolonged conversation, or gossip idly about informal matters.

Option meanings
• To chat idly — to talk in an informal, friendly manner without serious purpose [गपशप करना]
• To chew food — the literal mastication of food [खाना चबाना]
• To complain — to express dissatisfaction [शिकायत करना]
• To eat quickly — to devour food rapidly [तेजी से खाना]

Related words: Contextual equivalents: shoot the breeze, chit-chat, shoot the bull, jaw.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To put the cart before the horse [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: To do things in the wrong order

solution.en:
To put the cart before the horse [उल्टा काम करना, क्रम बिगाड़ना] is a classic idiom meaning to reverse the natural, logical, or sensible order of doing things.

Option meanings
• To do things in the wrong order — to perform tasks in reverse or illogical sequence [काम गलत क्रम में करना]
• To be very efficient — highly productive [अत्यधिक कुशल होना]

question.en:

A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: To hunt for rare birds in dense forests

2.en: To prefer guaranteed value over potential gain

3.en: To manage two projects at the same time

4.en: To take extreme risks to increase your wealth

solution.en:
A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush [नौ नकद न तेरह उधार, जो हाथ में है वह अनिश्चित से बेहतर है] is a proverbial idiom advising that it is much better to hold onto what one already possesses with certainty than to risk losing it by pursuing greater, uncertain prospective advantages.

Option meanings
• To prefer guaranteed value over potential gain — prioritizing assured possession over speculative prospects [निश्चित लाभ को प्राथमिकता देना]
• The other options provide literal or false interpretations.

question.en:

Absence makes the heart grow fonder [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: To travel far away to forget someone

2.en: To lose interest in a long-distance relationship

3.en: To value someone more when they are away

4.en: To feel sad when meeting new people

solution.en:

Option meanings

Therefore, To keep a safe distance from.

solution.en:

question.en: What does the idiom 'A storm in a teacup' mean? [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:

question.en: What does the idiom 'Burn bridges' mean? [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

question.en: What does the idiom 'Blow one's own trumpet' mean? [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

question.en: What does the idiom 'Cut the Gordian knot' mean? [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

question.en:
Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word:
The defendant was released on bail after the hearing. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: He paid bail to secure his friend's release from jail.

2.en: The judge set a high bail for the accused.

3.en: She rushed to the river to bail water out of the leaking boat.

4.en: The lawyer argued for a reduction in the client's bail.

solution.en:
In the given sentence, bail is a legal noun: the temporary release of an accused person on security [ज़मानत].

A homonym has the same spelling and sound but a different meaning. In option 3, bail means to scoop water out of a boat [नाव से पानी उलीचना].

Options 1, 2 and 4 use “bail” in the same legal sense as the question.

Answer: She rushed to the river to bail water out of the leaking boat.

question.en: Choose the correct sentence. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: She will bury the letter in the sand.

2.en: Please berry the box near the tree.

4.en: They berry the treasure every year.

solution.en:
Bury [दफनाना, गाड़ना] is a verb meaning to put something in the ground or hide it. Berry [बेर जैसा छोटा फल] is a noun — a small fruit.

Option 1 uses the verb correctly: She will bury the letter in the sand.

Options 2 and 4 use the noun “berry” as a verb, and option 3 uses the verb “bury” as something to eat.

question.en:

solution.en:
The clue describes the act of forming letters, so the word is write [लिखना].

right — correct; also a direction or an entitlement [सही, दायाँ, अधिकार]
rite — a ceremonial act [संस्कार, अनुष्ठान]
write — to form letters or words [लिखना]
wright — a maker or builder, as in playwright [निर्माता, शिल्पी]

These four words are homophones: they sound alike but differ in spelling and meaning.

question.en:
