question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
The cat suddenly jumped _____ the table and knocked _____ the cup. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Use onto, over.

Onto shows movement to a position on a surface: jumped onto the table.
Knock over means to push something so that it falls: knocked over the cup.

Complete sentence: The cat suddenly jumped onto the table and knocked over the cup.
[बिल्ली अचानक मेज़ पर कूदी और कप गिरा दिया।]

“Into”, “through” and “along” do not describe landing on a table top.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
Did she say anything _____ you _____ the interview? [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Use to, about.

Say something to someone names the listener, and about introduces the topic.

Complete sentence: Did she say anything to you about the interview?

The other pairs do not fit the pattern of “say”.

question.en:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:
The lawyer was intent _____ proving his client's innocence. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Use on.

The adjective intent (determined) takes on/upon + -ing: intent on proving.

Complete sentence: The lawyer was intent on proving his client's innocence.
[वकील अपने मुवक्किल की बेगुनाही साबित करने पर अडिग था।]

question.en:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:
She is skeptical _____ the results of the survey. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Use about.

Skeptical [संदेहशील] is followed by “about” or “of” to name the thing doubted.

Complete sentence: She is skeptical about the results of the survey.

question.en:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence.
The incident caused a rift ______ the two best friends. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Use between.

Between is used for two people or things; among for more than two. A rift “between the two best friends” involves exactly two people.

Complete sentence: The incident caused a rift between the two best friends.
[इस घटना ने दोनों पक्के दोस्तों के बीच दरार डाल दी।]

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully.
The poor fellow fell ______ his bicycle and landed ______ a puddle. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Use off, in.

Fall off a bicycle means to come down from it; land in a puddle means to end up in the water.

Complete sentence: The poor fellow fell off his bicycle and landed in a puddle.

In option 2, “landed into” is not idiomatic; options 3 and 4 are incorrect.

question.en:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:
The footfall has gone up ______ ten percent. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Use by.

By shows the amount or margin of a change: go up by ten percent.

Complete sentence: The footfall has gone up by ten percent.
[आगंतुकों की संख्या दस प्रतिशत बढ़ गई है।]

question.en:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:
She took the job ______ her parents' wishes. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Use against.

Against someone’s wishes [किसी की इच्छा के विरुद्ध] is the set phrase for doing something that another person opposes.

Complete sentence: She took the job against her parents' wishes.

“Inspite” is not a word (the phrase is “in spite of”), and “without” changes the meaning. “Despite” can show contrast in general English, but the fixed expression tested here is “against someone’s wishes”.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
The manager was alarmed ______ the delay and dissatisfied ______ the final outcome. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Use at, with.

Alarmed at [से चिंतित] is used for news or a situation that causes fear or worry.
Dissatisfied with [से असंतुष्ट] is the fixed pattern for the thing one is unhappy about.

Complete sentence: The manager was alarmed at the delay and dissatisfied with the final outcome.

“Dissatisfied about” and “dissatisfied by” are not standard, which rules out options 2 and 4; “alarmed at … dissatisfied with” is the standard adjective–preposition pairing tested here.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
The scientist explained the phenomenon in terms ______ quantum mechanics. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: The fixed phrase is "in terms of", meaning "with reference to" or "using the ideas of".

Correct sentence:
The scientist explained the phenomenon in terms of quantum mechanics.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
Only when the panel had concluded its year-long investigation ______ the depth of regulatory oversight failures become apparent. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: When a sentence begins with "Only when …", the main clause takes inversion (auxiliary + subject + verb). The time is past, so did … become is used.

Correct sentence:
Only when the panel had concluded its year-long investigation did the depth of regulatory oversight failures become apparent.

"Has", "had" and "was" do not go with the base form "become".

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
His critique of the narrative was not only grounded in textual exegesis but also ______ by a broader philosophical framework. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: "Not only … but also" must join parallel forms. "Grounded" is a past participle after "was", so the blank also needs a past participle: buttressed [समर्थित, सुदृढ़].

Correct sentence:
His critique of the narrative was not only grounded in textual exegesis but also buttressed by a broader philosophical framework.

"Buttresses" and "buttress" are present forms, and "buttressing" is a present participle, so none matches "grounded".

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
The memorandum was neither meticulously structured nor ______ proofread, leading to interpretive confusion. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: "Neither … nor" must join parallel forms. "Meticulously structured" is adverb + past participle, so the blank needs an adverb before "proofread": adequately [पर्याप्त रूप से].

Correct sentence:
The memorandum was neither meticulously structured nor adequately proofread, leading to interpretive confusion.

"Adequateness" and "adequacy" are nouns, and "adequate" is an adjective.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correct option.
She ______ like to come with us. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: "Would like to" is the polite way of expressing a wish. "Like" is a base verb, so it needs the modal would.

Correct sentence:
She would like to come with us.

"Do" and "is" do not agree with "she" here, and "will like to" is not the idiomatic form for a polite wish.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correct option.
Neither of the solutions ______ suitable for the problem. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: "Neither of" + plural noun takes a singular verb, because "neither" means "not either one".

Correct sentence:
Neither of the solutions is suitable for the problem.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
The judge ruled ______ favour of the plaintiff and passed judgment ______ the defendant. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: The fixed phrases are "rule in favour of" (decide in support of) and "pass judgment against" (decide against someone).

Correct sentence:
The judge ruled in favour of the plaintiff and passed judgment against the defendant.

question.en:
Choose the best option to fill in the blanks.
This is ____ biryani I have had in a year. It is almost ____ the one from Nizam's House in Hyderabad. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
Blank 1: comparing this biryani with all the biryanis eaten in a year needs the superlative with "the" → the best.
Blank 2: equality is shown by as + positive adjective + as → as good as.
"Gooder" is not a word, "the better" does not fit the first blank, and "better" without "than" is incomplete.

Correct sentence:
This is the best biryani I have had in a year. It is almost as good as the one from Nizam's House in Hyderabad.

question.en:
Choose the best option to fill in the blanks.
There was ___ robbery in ___ university campus. ___ thief entered ___ boys' hostel and took away ___ laptop. ___ FIR was lodged by ___ Principal. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

1.en: a, the, a, the, a, an, the

2.en: a, the, the, the, a, a, the

3.en: the, the, the, the, the, the, a

4.en: a, a, a, the, the, a, the

solution.en:
Rule
a/an is used for something mentioned for the first time (not specific); the is used for something specific or already known.
a robbery — first mention
the university campus — a particular campus
a thief — first mention, an unknown person
the boys' hostel — the particular hostel of that campus
a laptop — any one laptop, first mention
an FIR — "F" is pronounced "ef" (vowel sound), so an
the Principal — the particular principal of that university

Correct sentence:
There was a robbery in the university campus. A thief entered the boys' hostel and took away a laptop. An FIR was lodged by the Principal.

Hence the answer is a, the, a, the, a, an, the.

question.en:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.
The ______ rose as the fog cleared. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Sun [सूर्य] fits the meaning: the sun rose as the fog cleared.
The options are similar-sounding words, so the choice depends on meaning.

Correct sentence:
The sun rose as the fog cleared.

Option meanings
Sun — the star that gives Earth light and heat [सूर्य]
Son — a male child [पुत्र]
Sin — a wrong or immoral act [पाप]
Soon — in a short time [जल्द ही]

question.en:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:
_____ being a teacher, he is also a musician. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: Besides means "in addition to" [के अतिरिक्त]; beside means "next to" [के बगल में]. The sentence adds another role (musician) to his being a teacher, so Besides is correct.

Correct sentence:
Besides being a teacher, he is also a musician.

"With" and "after" do not give the meaning "in addition to".

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully
He excelled _____ academics and stood out _____ his remarkable leadership skills. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
Excel in a field or subject [किसी क्षेत्र में उत्कृष्ट होना] → excelled in academics.
Stand out for a quality [किसी गुण के कारण अलग दिखना] → stood out for his leadership skills.

Correct sentence:
He excelled in academics and stood out for his remarkable leadership skills.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
His views were incompatible ____ the team’s values and detrimental ____ overall progress. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
Incompatible with [से असंगत] and detrimental to [के लिए हानिकारक] are fixed adjective–preposition pairs.

Correct sentence:
His views were incompatible with the team's values and detrimental to overall progress.

question.en: The leader’s speech was deliberately ______, allowing different groups to interpret it in their own way. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Ambiguous [अस्पष्ट, द्व्यर्थक] means open to more than one interpretation. The clue is "allowing different groups to interpret it in their own way".

Correct sentence:
The leader's speech was deliberately ambiguous, allowing different groups to interpret it in their own way.

Option meanings
Precise — exact and clear [सटीक]
Ambiguous — having more than one possible meaning [द्व्यर्थक]
Decisive — settling an issue firmly [निर्णायक]
Explicit — stated clearly and in detail [स्पष्ट]

question.en: The school authorities ______ several measures to improve student safety over the past few months. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: "Over the past few months" shows an action spread over a period that continues up to the present, so the present perfect (has/have + V3) is used. "Authorities" is plural → have introduced.

Correct sentence:
The school authorities have introduced several measures to improve student safety over the past few months.

"Introduce" is simple present, "introduced" (simple past) does not suit a period continuing up to now, and "had introduced" needs another past action for reference.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correct option.
The company is known ______ its excellent customer service. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: known for is used for the quality or reason for which someone or something is famous.

Correct sentence:
The company is known for its excellent customer service.

Known as introduces a name or title, known to means familiar to someone, and known by means identified by something.

sets.title: SSC 2026 FILL IN THE BLANKS PART-2

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the correct option.
You must ______ your passport at the airport before departure. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The modal must is followed by the base form of the verb.

Correct sentence:
You must show your passport at the airport before departure.

"showed" (past), "showing" (-ing form) and "shown" (past participle) cannot follow a modal directly.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully.
I baked this cake especially ______ you ______ celebrate your promotion. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule
for shows the person who benefits from an action, and the to-infinitive shows purpose.

especially for you → the cake is meant for "you"
to celebrate → purpose of baking

Correct sentence:
I baked this cake especially for you to celebrate your promotion.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully.
She painted the wall ______ a roller ______ a brush. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule
with introduces the instrument used to do something, and instead of means "in place of".

Correct sentence:
She painted the wall with a roller instead of a brush.

"by, without", "from, to" and "for, with" do not express the instrument-and-replacement meaning.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
He is ______ doubt the perfect candidate ______ this job. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule
without doubt [निःसंदेह] is a fixed phrase meaning "certainly", and one is a candidate for a job.

Correct sentence:
He is without doubt the perfect candidate for this job.

"with doubt", "for doubt" and "above doubt … in this job" are not correct here.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
The new intern was entrusted ______ critical files and tasked ______ compiling the monthly report. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule
One is entrusted with something [किसी को कुछ सौंपना], and tasked with doing something (tasked with + V-ing).

Correct sentence:
The new intern was entrusted with critical files and tasked with compiling the monthly report.

"in, to", "on, by" and "of, of" are wrong prepositions with these verbs.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
We were warned ______ potential delays and advised ______ carry extra provisions. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule
One is warned of (or about) a danger, and advised to + base verb.

Correct sentence:
We were warned of potential delays and advised to carry extra provisions.

"about, for", "for, on" and "at, in" do not fit; "advised" needs the to-infinitive here.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
She sat ______ the fireplace ______ keep warm. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct pair is near, to.

Near shows position close to something, and to introduces the purpose (to keep warm).

Correct sentence: She sat near the fireplace to keep warm.

"Below/above the fireplace" does not make sense, and "from/with keep warm" is ungrammatical.

question.en:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:
My house is just one-kilometre ______ the beach. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct preposition is from.

Distance is measured from a place: one kilometre from the beach.

Correct sentence: My house is just one kilometre from the beach.

"To", "of" and "till" do not express distance from a point.

question.en:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:
We heard the unfortunate news ______ the radio. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct preposition is over.

We hear news over (or on) the radio, meaning through the medium of radio.

Correct sentence: We heard the unfortunate news over the radio.

"In", "from" and "at" the radio are not idiomatic here.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
The book is divided ______ five parts and dedicated ______ the author's parents. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct pair is into, to.

Something is divided into parts, and a book is dedicated to a person.

Correct sentence: The book is divided into five parts and dedicated to the author's parents.

"Divided among" is used for sharing between people, and "dedicated for" is wrong.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
The policy is inconsistent ______ the company's values and incompatible ______ our long-term goals. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct pair is with, with.

Both inconsistent and incompatible take the preposition with.

Correct sentence: The policy is inconsistent with the company's values and incompatible with our long-term goals.

question.en:
Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
The climbers reached the ______ of the mountain by dawn. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Peak [शिखर, चोटी] is the top of a mountain.

Option meanings
peek — a quick, secret look [झाँकना]
peak — the summit of a mountain [चोटी]
pique — irritation; to arouse interest [चिढ़; जिज्ञासा जगाना]
pick — to choose [चुनना]

Correct sentence: The climbers reached the peak of the mountain by dawn.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
This poem is ______ the collection 'Gitanjali' ______ Rabindranath Tagore. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The correct pair is from, by.

From shows the source (the collection), and by shows the author.

Correct sentence: This poem is from the collection 'Gitanjali' by Rabindranath Tagore.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully.
He worked ______ the night ______ finish the project. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The correct pair is through, to.

Through the night means continuously from the beginning to the end of the night, and to + verb shows purpose (to finish).

Correct sentence: He worked through the night to finish the project.

"For finish", "without finish" and "towards finish" are ungrammatical before a bare verb.

question.en:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:
They insisted ______ paying the full amount in advance. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Insist [ज़ोर देना, आग्रह करना] takes the preposition on: insist on + noun/gerund.

Correct sentence: They insisted on paying the full amount in advance.

question.en:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:
She takes great pride ______ her work. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Take pride in [पर गर्व करना] is the fixed collocation, while "be proud of" takes "of".

Correct sentence: She takes great pride in her work.

question.en:
Choose the correct word.
He made a _____ comment during the meeting. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Examine the meanings of these homophones:
• Coarse [अशिष्ट, खुरदरा, अभद्र] — rough in texture, or vulgar, crude, and impolite in manners or speech (fitting the context of an offensive remark: 'a coarse comment').
• Course [मार्ग, पाठ्यक्रम, क्रम] — the route of travel, a programme of study, or part of a meal.
• Corse — an archaic poetic word for a dead human body (corpse).
• Cores — plural of core; central central portions of fruit or objects.
Therefore, the appropriate word is coarse.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
I saw him going _____ the temple _____ a car. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Prepositional Analysis:
1. First blank: 'going past the temple' means moving physically along a path that leads beyond the temple [मंदिर के आगे से गुजरना].
2. Second blank: To indicate travel inside a personal automobile/taxi, the standard preposition is in ('in a car'), whereas 'by' is used without an article ('by car').

Complete sentence: I saw him going past the temple in a car.

The other options violate either directional logic or vehicle preposition rules.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
He packed his bags and left _____ dawn _____ saying a word. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Prepositional Analysis:
1. First blank: Specific exact times of day such as 'dawn', 'dusk', 'noon', and 'midnight' take the fixed temporal preposition at: 'at dawn' [भोर के समय].
2. Second blank: The preposition without followed by a gerund expresses absence of an action: 'without saying a word' [बिना एक शब्द बोले].

Complete sentence: He packed his bags and left at dawn without saying a word.

Combinations with 'in', 'on', or 'for' are grammatically unidiomatic with 'dawn'.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
She was entrusted _____ an important task and praised _____ her dedication. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Prepositional Collocations:
1. First blank: The verb entrust follows the fixed construction entrust someone with something: 'entrusted with an important task' [महत्वपूर्ण कार्य सौंपा जाना].
2. Second blank: The verb praise follows the construction praise someone for something: 'praised for her dedication' [समर्पण के लिए सराहना करना].

Complete sentence: She was entrusted with an important task and praised for her dedication.

Therefore, the correct pair of prepositions is with, for.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
His actions stem _____ ignorance and result _____ widespread confusion. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Prepositional Collocations:
1. First blank: The phrasal verb stem from [से उत्पन्न होना] means to originate or arise as a consequence of something: 'stem from ignorance'.
2. Second blank: The phrasal verb result in [में परिणत होना, का कारण बनना] means to cause or culminate in a specific outcome: 'result in widespread confusion'.

Complete sentence: His actions stem from ignorance and result in widespread confusion.

Therefore, the correct set of prepositions is from, in.

question.en:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:
The poor children gathered ______ the food truck. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
“Around” means on every side of something; children gathering on all sides of the truck.
Sentence: The poor children gathered around the food truck.

Other options
Along = following a line; among = in the middle of many (a group), not a single object; above = higher than.

Therefore, around.

question.en:
Choose the most suitable preposition from the given options to fill in the blank in the following sentence:
______ other things, the boy is a talented singer and guitarist. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
“Among other things” is a fixed expression meaning “in addition to other things”.
Sentence: Among other things, the boy is a talented singer and guitarist.

Other options
Along, Across and Between do not form this expression (“between” is used for two items).

Therefore, Among.

question.en:
The following sentence has two blanks. Choose the most suitable set of prepositions from the given options to fill in the blanks and complete the sentence meaningfully:
They were engaged ______ negotiations and hopeful ______ a positive outcome. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Fixed prepositions
engaged in (an activity) – engaged in negotiations.
hopeful for (a result) – hopeful for a positive outcome.
Sentence: They were engaged in negotiations and hopeful for a positive outcome.
Other pairs (at/of, with/in, on/of) do not fit these collocations.

Therefore, in, for.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
Of the two candidates, the younger one is ______. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: When comparing two persons or things, use the comparative degree (often with “the” before “of the two”).
“Of the two candidates” → comparative “more talented”.
Correct: Of the two candidates, the younger one is more talented.
“most / the most talented” are superlatives (for three or more); “talented” alone makes no comparison.

Therefore, more talented.

sets.title: SSC 2026 FILL IN THE BLANKS PART-3

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
The ______ of the antique vase was estimated to be in the millions. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
After the article “The” and before “of the antique vase”, a noun is required.
“value” (noun) = worth. The value … was estimated to be in the millions.
valuable (adjective), valuing (gerund/participle) and valued (past participle) do not fit as the subject noun.

Therefore, value.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
The diplomat was known for his ______ approach, always choosing words that would not offend anyone. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The clue “always choosing words that would not offend anyone” describes a person who handles situations with sensitivity – “tactful”.
Blunt, harsh and rigid are the opposite qualities.

Therefore, tactful.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
She was charged ______ negligence in handling confidential files. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** The verb **charge** takes the fixed preposition **with** when referring to an accusation or formal offense (**charged with something**).
**Correct sentence:** She was charged **with** negligence in handling confidential files.
Prepositions **for**, **of**, and **on** do not form the standard idiomatic collocation with **charge** in this context.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The agreement was subject ______ approval by the director. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** The phrase **subject to** is a fixed idiomatic adjective phrase meaning dependent on or conditional upon something.
**Correct sentence:** The agreement was subject **to** approval by the director.
Options (a), (b), and (d) do not complete the required standard phrasal collocation **subject to**.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
Despite the storm, the climbers pressed ______ the treacherous path with unwavering resolve. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** The phrasal verb **press on** means to continue moving forward or making progress determinedly despite hardships.
**Correct sentence:** Despite the storm, the climbers pressed **on** the treacherous path with unwavering resolve.
Options (b), (c), and (d) do not complete the intended phrasal idiom *press on*.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
She has been working here, ______ ten years without a single day off. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** In present perfect continuous constructions, **for** denotes a duration or period of time (**ten years**), whereas *since* is reserved for a specific point in time.
**Correct sentence:** She has been working here, **for** ten years without a single day off.
Options (a), (b), and (c) violate the rules governing time expressions in perfect tenses.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
The policy's deployment of econometric models, while statistically robust, remains normatively ______, eliding key ethical questions. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Meaning:** **Untenable** means not able to be defended against criticism or objection.
Because the econometric models ignore critical ethical questions, the policy's normative position cannot be sustained.
Options (a), (b), and (c) do not logically fit the semantic context of normative ethics.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
The ambassador's statement, riddled with diplomatic hedging, failed to offer a ______ position on the escalating conflict. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** The noun **position** must be modified by an adjective; **categorical** means unambiguous, explicit, and direct.
**Correct sentence:** ...failed to offer a **categorical** position on the escalating conflict.
Option (a) is a verb, (b) is an adverb, and (c) is a noun.

question.en:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
He is endowed ______ exceptional memory. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
The fixed collocation is “endowed with” (to be given a quality or possession).

Explicit changes
The blank takes the preposition “with”.

Final sentence
He is endowed with exceptional memory.

“Endowed of/for/by” are not standard English collocations.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
His argument lacks coherence and is filled with logical ______. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
A lack of coherence with faulty reasoning is filled with logical fallacies (mistaken arguments).

Option meanings
paradoxes — apparent contradictions [विरोधाभास]
incoherents — not a standard noun here
fallacies — flawed reasoning [तर्कदोष]
digresses — verb, not a noun

Final sentence: His argument lacks coherence and is filled with logical fallacies.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
If she ______ more attention in class, she would have passed easily. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
Third conditional: If + past perfect, ... would have + past participle (an unreal past).

Explicit changes
The result clause “would have passed” requires “had paid” in the if-clause.

Final sentence
If she had paid more attention in class, she would have passed easily.

“Pays”, “has paid” and “would pay” do not form a third conditional.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
If he ______ earlier, we could have caught the express train. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
Third conditional: If + past perfect, ... could have + past participle.

Explicit changes
The result “could have caught” requires “had arrived” in the if-clause.

Final sentence
If he had arrived earlier, we could have caught the express train.

“Was arriving”, “arrives” and “would arrive” do not form this unreal-past conditional.

question.en:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option:
The theory remained ______ the fringes of academic discourse until empirical validation emerged. [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
The fixed collocation is “on the fringes” (at the outer edge of something).

Explicit changes
The blank takes the preposition “on”.

Final sentence
The theory remained on the fringes of academic discourse until empirical validation emerged.

“Of/at/by the fringes” are not standard collocations here.

question.en:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.
The ________ nature of the coral reef makes it highly susceptible to changes in water temperature. [Selection Post (Graduate) 22 Sep 2026 Shift 1]
question.hi:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.

Rule: The verb appeal takes the preposition to when referring to the person or authority being addressed (appeal to somebody for something).
Correct sentence: "The villagers appealed to the authorities for immediate help."

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
He arrived right in time. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Right on time is correct.

“On time” means punctually, at the scheduled moment; “in time” means early enough, before it is too late. The sentence describes punctual arrival, and “right” naturally intensifies “on time”.

Correct sentence: He arrived right on time.
[वह बिल्कुल ठीक समय पर पहुँचा।]

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
The new girl came and sat besides me in class. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Use beside.

Beside [के बगल में] means next to; besides [के अलावा] means in addition to. “Of” is not used after either word here.

Correct sentence: The new girl came and sat beside me in class.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
The company was charged on violating environmental laws. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Use charged with.

When “charge” means to accuse someone formally of an offence, it takes “with”: be charged with an offence or with doing something.

Correct sentence: The company was charged with violating environmental laws.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
She was adding to the confusion by making contradictory statements. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
No substitution is required.

Add to [बढ़ाना] means to increase something. “Adding to the confusion” correctly means making the confusion greater.

“Add with”, “add in” and “add on” do not give this meaning here.

Correct sentence: She was adding to the confusion by making contradictory statements.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
The teacher directed the students to submit their assignments before the deadline. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

3.en: directed to the students to submit

solution.en:
No substitution is required.

In the sense of instructing, direct + person + to-infinitive is the correct pattern: directed the students to submit.

The other options use a wrong preposition or put “to” before the object.

Correct sentence: The teacher directed the students to submit their assignments before the deadline.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
My car accidentally went over a small dog. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Use ran over.

Run over [कुचल देना] means to hit someone or something with a vehicle and pass over it. “Went over” means examined or crossed, “drove on” means continued driving, and “passed up on” means declined an opportunity.

Correct sentence: My car accidentally ran over a small dog.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
The suspect is currently under custody, while the police continue their investigation. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

In custody [हिरासत में] is the fixed phrase for being held by the police.

Correct sentence: The suspect is currently in custody, while the police continue their investigation.

question.en:

solution.en:

Get on with [काम में लगे रहना, आगे बढ़ाना] means to continue or make progress with a task.

question.en:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is bolded. Choose the correct alternative that best improves the bolded part.
The executive council has reached to a unanimous decision regarding the acquisition of the rival firm after months of negotiation. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Use has reached.

“Reach” takes a direct object without “to”: reach a decision. “The executive council” is a singular collective noun here, so “has” is correct.

Correct sentence: The executive council has reached a unanimous decision regarding the acquisition of the rival firm after months of negotiation.

question.en:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is bolded. Choose the correct alternative that best improves the bolded part.
She is considered the most intelligent of the two architects who designed the sustainable skyscraper project for the new business district. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

2.en: the more intelligent of the two

solution.en:
Use the more intelligent of the two.

When exactly two people are compared, use the comparative (more) with “the … of the two”; the superlative (most) is for three or more.

Correct sentence: She is considered the more intelligent of the two architects who designed the sustainable skyscraper project for the new business district.

question.en:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is bolded. Choose the correct alternative that best improves the bolded part.
I prefer to analyze the raw data personally to relying on the subjective interpretations provided by the junior researchers. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Prefer compares two actions with the pattern prefer + -ing … to + -ing; “prefer … than” is not standard.
The sentence already has “to relying”, so the first action should also be a gerund: “analyzing”.

Correct sentence: I prefer analyzing the raw data personally to relying on the subjective interpretations provided by the junior researchers.

Therefore, the best improvement is I prefer analyzing.

question.en:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
The committee concluded that the proposal was not acceptable nor was it feasible for implementation. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: not acceptable nor was it feasible

solution.en:
Rule: "Nor" pairs with "neither", not with "not". The correlative pair must join parallel words: neither acceptable nor feasible.

Correct sentence:
The committee concluded that the proposal was neither acceptable nor feasible for implementation.

Option 3 is grammatical but wordy, and option 4 wrongly pairs "unacceptable" with "nor" and gives the opposite meaning with "unfeasible".

question.en:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
He is more senior than me in the organization. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: Senior, junior, superior, inferior and prior take "to", not "than", and are not used with "more".

Correct sentence:
He is senior to me in the organization.

"More senior to I" uses "more" and the wrong pronoun, "senior than me" uses "than", and "more senior than" keeps both errors.

question.en:
Choose the option that best improves the given sentence for correct grammar and clarity.
He did not came to the meeting yesterday. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: He did not came to the meeting yesterday.

2.en: He did not come to the meeting yesterday.

3.en: He did not coming to the meeting yesterday.

4.en: He not came to the meeting yesterday.

solution.en:
Rule: "Did" / "did not" is always followed by the base form (V1) of the verb.
So "did not came" becomes "did not come".

Correct sentence:
He did not come to the meeting yesterday.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
We stayed in home all day and watched movies. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

Correct sentence:
We stayed at home all day and watched movies.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
The cab turned to an alley to avoid the traffic jam. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

Correct sentence:

question.en:

solution.en:
Stand up to [डटकर मुकाबला करना] means to resist or confront someone powerful. This is exactly what is needed against bullies, so no substitution is required.

Option meanings

Stand up with — not an idiomatic phrase in this sense
Stand up as — not an idiomatic phrase in this sense

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
He has become over-confident, as he was able to get over with cheating on the last test. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: Get away with means to escape punishment for doing something wrong [बच निकलना]. He became over-confident because he escaped punishment for cheating.

Correct sentence:
He has become over-confident, as he was able to get away with cheating on the last test.

Option meanings
Get around with — not a standard phrasal verb with this meaning ("get around" = travel or avoid) [टालना]
Get away with — to escape punishment [बच निकलना]
Get off with — to receive only a light punishment [हल्की सज़ा पाकर छूटना]
Get over with (given phrase) — "get something over with" = to finish an unpleasant task [निपटा देना]

question.en:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is bolded. Choose the correct alternative that best improves the bolded part.
I completed the report before the senior manager entered the office to request the final figures for the board presentation. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: When two actions happened in the past, the action completed first takes the past perfect (had + V3), and the later action takes the simple past. The report was completed before the manager entered.

Correct sentence:
I had completed the report before the senior manager entered the office to request the final figures for the board presentation.

"Have finished" is present perfect, "was finishing" shows an unfinished action, and "had finish" is an incorrect verb form (it needs V3, "finished").

question.en:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is bolded. Choose the correct alternative that best improves the bolded part.
He is superior than his contemporaries in the field of theoretical physics and quantum mechanics due to his innovative research. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: Latin comparatives such as superior, inferior, senior, junior and prior take "to", not "than", and are never used with "more" or "most".

Correct sentence:
He is superior to his contemporaries in the field of theoretical physics and quantum mechanics due to his innovative research.

"More superior to" and "most superior than" double the comparison, and "superior from" uses the wrong preposition.

question.en:
Select the grammatically correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.
The lead soloist sings very beautiful in the regional choir. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: A verb is modified by an adverb, not an adjective. "Sings" is a verb, so the adverb beautifully is needed; "very" modifies the adverb.

Correct sentence:
The lead soloist sings very beautifully in the regional choir.

"Beauty" is a noun, and "sang very beautiful" changes the tense and still uses the adjective.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

solution.en:
Rule: look out of the window means to look from inside, through the window, to the outside.

Correct sentence:
She looked out of the window to see the view of the garden.

"look in the window" means looking into a place from outside, "look to" means to rely on, and "look up the window" is meaningless.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
The total amount earned with the sale exceeded expectations. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: earn from shows the source of income or profit.

Correct sentence:
The total amount earned from the sale exceeded expectations.

"earned with", "earned of" and "earned to" are not correct collocations.

question.en:

Correct sentence:
He completed the project primarily through hard work and dedication.

"with" suggests an instrument or accompaniment, and "from" suggests origin, so neither fits as naturally.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

Correct sentence:
We need to formulate a plan of action before the project commences.

"plan on action", "plan for action" and "plan in action" are not idiomatic.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
I am really looking forward to meeting my friends this weekend. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: In look forward to, "to" is a preposition, so it is followed by a gerund (V-ing). The given sentence "looking forward to meeting" is already correct, so no substitution is required.

Look at — to see or observe [देखना]
Look up to — to admire or respect [आदर करना]
Look forward for — incorrect preposition
Look forward to — to wait eagerly for [उत्सुकता से प्रतीक्षा करना]

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
The committee members are looking at the matter to find a solution. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

Rule: look into means to investigate or examine [जाँच करना]. A committee trying to find a solution examines the matter.

Correct sentence:
The committee members are looking into the matter to find a solution.

Option meanings
Look at — to observe [देखना]
Look into — to investigate [जाँच करना]
Look up — to search for information in a reference [खोजना]
Look for — to search for something lost [ढूँढना]

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution'.
They decided to go ahead with the new venture despite of the challenges. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct phrase is in spite of.

Rule: Use either despite (without "of") or in spite of. "Despite of", "in despite of" and "in spite for" are wrong.

Correct sentence: They decided to go ahead with the new venture in spite of the challenges.

question.en:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is bolded. Choose the correct alternative that best improves the bolded part.
Unless the regulators do not intervene in the proposed corporate merger, the resulting monopoly will stifle all local competition and innovation. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct phrase is Unless the regulators.

Rule: Unless already means "if not", so it must not be followed by another "not". "Unless ... do not" is a double negative.

Correct sentence: Unless the regulators intervene in the proposed corporate merger, the resulting monopoly will stifle all local competition and innovation.

question.en:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is bolded. Choose the correct alternative that best improves the bolded part.
I will depart immediately, mustn't I, to avoid missing the final flight connection to the international conference in London? [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct phrase is I must depart immediately.

Rule: A modal (must) is followed by the base form of the verb (depart). "Will depart, mustn't I" mixes two auxiliaries wrongly, and "must have/been/had depart" are ungrammatical.

Correct sentence: I must depart immediately to avoid missing the final flight connection to the international conference in London.

question.en:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is bolded. Choose the correct alternative that best improves the bolded part.
The pilot had been more vigilant regarding the weather reports, the emergency landing could have been successfully averted. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct phrase is Had the pilot been.

Rule: In a third conditional (past unreal condition), "If the pilot had been" can be written with inversion as Had the pilot been; the main clause uses could have + past participle.

Correct sentence: Had the pilot been more vigilant regarding the weather reports, the emergency landing could have been successfully averted.

question.en:
Select the grammatically correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No improvement'.
Having practised all week, she tells the story confidently at the competition yesterday. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The correct phrase is told the story confidently.

Rule: The time marker yesterday requires the simple past (told). Present, present continuous and present perfect cannot be used with "yesterday".

Correct sentence: Having practised all week, she told the story confidently at the competition yesterday.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
The car was parked right out the gate, blocking the driveway. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

3.en: in the front of the gate

solution.en:
In front of [के सामने] is the correct phrase for position. "Right out the gate" is an informal idiom meaning "immediately, from the very start", not a location.

Correct sentence: The car was parked in front of the gate, blocking the driveway.

"In front to" is ungrammatical, and "in the front of" means "in the front part inside something".

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
The general was entrusted for the safety of the troops. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: We entrust someone with something (or entrust something to someone). Here the person (the general) is the subject, so entrusted with is correct.

Correct sentence: The general was entrusted with the safety of the troops.

"Entrusted by" would introduce the doer, and "entrusted to" needs the thing as subject: The safety of the troops was entrusted to the general.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
The company is currently under threat from a potential lawsuit. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule:
Under threat of + the harmful action that may happen (closure, legal action, a lawsuit).
Under threat from + the source of the danger (rivals, floods, poachers).

A lawsuit is the action that may happen to the company, so under threat of is correct.

Correct sentence: The company is currently under threat of a potential lawsuit.

"Under threat by" and "on threat from" are not idiomatic.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
The travellers met off an accident on the way. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Meet with [(दुर्घटना आदि) का शिकार होना] is used for experiencing an accident, success, failure or opposition.

Correct sentence: The travellers met with an accident on the way.

"Met off" and "met of" are not phrases, and "met an accident" is not used.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
The doctor has advised me to cut down in my sugar intake to stay healthy. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Cut down on [कम करना] means to reduce the amount of something one uses or consumes.

Correct sentence: The doctor has advised me to cut down on my sugar intake to stay healthy.

"Cut off" means to disconnect or stop a supply, and "cut down for/in" are not idiomatic.

question.en:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is bolded. Choose the correct alternative that best improves the bolded part.
The new fiscal amendments have had a significant affect on the purchasing power of the middle class during this period of deflation. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Effect [प्रभाव] is a noun and affect [प्रभावित करना] is a verb. After "a significant", a noun is needed, so effect. The subject "amendments" is plural, so have had is correct.

Correct sentence: The new fiscal amendments have had a significant effect on the purchasing power of the middle class during this period of deflation.

Option 1 uses "has" with a plural subject and keeps "affect", option 2 is ungrammatical, and option 4 drops the article and changes the tense.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
He takes pride for his cultural heritage. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule on Fixed Prepositions:
• The noun 'pride' in the idiomatic expression 'take pride in' always takes the preposition in: to take pride in something [किसी बात पर गर्व करना].
• In contrast, when used as a reflexive verb, it takes 'on': he prides himself on his work.
• 'Pride for' and 'pride of' are grammatically incorrect in this verbal construction.

Correct sentence: He takes pride in his cultural heritage.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
She is skilled at playing both the piano and the violin. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule on Prepositional Collocation:
The adjective skilled is idiomatically followed by the preposition at (or in) when designating an activity or talent: skilled at doing something / skilled in a trade.
The phrases 'skilled for', 'skilled to', and 'skilled on' violate standard English usage.
Therefore, No substitution is required.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'
The new policies have led in a significant increase in productivity. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: The phrasal verb lead to [का कारण बनना, परिणत होना] means to result in or culminate in a particular consequence. Its past participle is 'led to'.

Correct sentence: The new policies have led to a significant increase in productivity.

Were the testimony verified by independent witnesses today, the jury would likely have returned a vastly different verdict in the criminal case. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Conditional Sentence Rule:
• Look at the main clause: 'the jury would likely have returned a vastly different verdict' (would have + V3).
• This requires a Third Conditional (Past Unreal Counterfactual) in the if-clause: If + subject + had been + V3, or in inverted form without 'if': 'Had the testimony been verified...'.
• 'Were the testimony verified' is a second conditional inversion, which would incorrectly require 'would return', not 'would have returned'.

Correct sentence: Had the testimony been verified by independent witnesses, the jury would likely have returned a vastly different verdict...

solution.en:
Transitive Verb Pattern Rule:
The verb explain does not take a double object (it cannot be followed directly by an indirect object of person: *explain someone something is ungrammatical). Correct sentence: The sociology professor explained to me the intricate societal dynamics...

A. the kitchen
B. brewed coffee fills
C. every morning
D. the aroma of freshly [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:

question.en:
In the following question, the first and last parts of the sentence (1 and 6) are given. The rest of the sentence is split into four parts and named P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence and find out which of the four combinations is correct.

1. Renewable energy investments
P. as the government
Q. have increased substantially
R. on imported fossil fuels
S. seeks to reduce dependence
6. to improve national energy security. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Correct order: QPSR

Renewable energy investments + Q "have increased substantially" (verb)
P "as the government" (reason clause begins)
S "seeks to reduce dependence"
R "on imported fossil fuels" (dependence on)

Final sentence
Renewable energy investments have increased substantially as the government seeks to reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels to improve national energy security.

B. long summer afternoons
C. re-reading my favourite childhood story
D. spent in the quiet garden [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Sentence Structure Analysis:
1. Part C: 're-reading my favourite childhood story' acts as the gerund subject of the sentence.
2. Part A: 'brought back many warm memories of' is the main predicate verb phrase taking a prepositional object.
3. Part B: 'long summer afternoons' acts as the noun object of the preposition 'of'.
4. Part D: 'spent in the quiet garden' is a past-participial modifier describing the afternoons.

Complete meaningful sentence: Re-reading my favourite childhood story brought back many warm memories of long summer afternoons spent in the quiet garden.

Put subject + verb + complement + adverb in order.

Explicit changes
C (the garden) + B (bloomed) + A (with red flowers) + D (beautifully).

CBAD is the only option that yields a meaningful sentence.

question.en:
Arrange the sentence parts:
(A) in the evening (B) the guests (C) arrived (D) at the venue [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
Arrange as subject + verb + place + time — the natural English order.

Explicit arrangement
B “the guests” — the subject opens the sentence.
C “arrived” — the verb follows the subject.
D “at the venue” — the place phrase follows the verb.
A “in the evening” — the time phrase closes the sentence.

Final sentence
The guests arrived at the venue in the evening.

BACD gives “The guests in the evening arrived at the venue”, which breaks the subject–verb flow; BADC and ACBD are also unnatural.
Therefore, BCDA.

question.en:
Arrange the sentence parts:
(A) for her success (B) congratulated (C) they (D) the candidate [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
Arrange as subject + verb + object + reason.

Explicit arrangement
C “they” — the subject opens the sentence.
B “congratulated” — the verb follows.
D “the candidate” — the object of “congratulated”.
A “for her success” — the reason phrase closes the sentence.

Final sentence
They congratulated the candidate for her success.

CBAD gives “They congratulated for her success the candidate”, separating the verb from its object; ABDC and DBAC do not start with the subject.
Therefore, CBDA.

question.en:
In the following question, the sentence has been split into four parts. These parts are jumbled and not in the correct order. Select the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence.
A. She loves to read
B. during the evening
C. by the window
D. old mystery novels [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule
Arrange as subject + verb + object + time + place.

Explicit arrangement
A “She loves to read” — subject and verb open the sentence.
D “old mystery novels” — the object must come directly after “read”.
B “during the evening” — the time phrase.
C “by the window” — the place phrase completes the sentence.

Final sentence
She loves to read old mystery novels during the evening by the window.

ABDC gives “She loves to read during the evening old mystery novels…”, wrongly separating the verb “read” from its object “old mystery novels”; DABC and CBAD do not begin with the subject.
Therefore, ADBC.

Order: B, A, D, C forms: "Scientists study Antarctica to understand Earth's past and future."

question.en:

takes students (A) / this scholarship programme (B) / to remote parts (C) / of the world (D) [Selection Post (12th) 26 Sep 2026 Shift 1]
question.hi:
Given below are four jumbled parts of a sentence. Select the option that gives their correct order and forms a meaningful sentence.
takes students (A) / this scholarship programme (B) / to remote parts (C) / of the world (D) [Selection Post (12th) 26 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Sentence Structure:

ecological consequences (A) / lead to major (B) / minor environmental (C) / changes can (D) [Selection Post (12th) 26 Sep 2026 Shift 1]
question.hi:

ecological consequences (A) / lead to major (B) / minor environmental (C) / changes can (D) [Selection Post (12th) 26 Sep 2026 Shift 1]
