question.en:
Choose the part of the sentence that contains an error:
She is senior than me by five years. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is senior than; use senior to.

Latin comparatives ending in -ior (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) take “to”, not “than”.

Correct sentence: She is senior to me by five years.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The novelist who her editor had praised (1)/ for stylistic ingenuity and metaphorical clarity (2)/ was yet to submit (3)/ the final chapters of the manuscript. (4) [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is in part (1): who should be whom.

In the relative clause, “her editor” is the subject, and the relative pronoun is the object of “had praised”; the object form is “whom”.

Correct sentence: The novelist whom her editor had praised for stylistic ingenuity and metaphorical clarity was yet to submit the final chapters of the manuscript.

Check: “her editor had praised her” — an object form, so “whom”.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Scholars in postcolonial studies (1)/ often disputes the neutrality (2)/ of archival records (3)/ and the politics of naming. (4) [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is in part (2): disputes should be dispute.

The subject is the plural noun “scholars”; “in postcolonial studies” only describes them. A plural subject takes a plural verb.

Correct sentence: Scholars in postcolonial studies often dispute the neutrality of archival records and the politics of naming.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
Qatar has extended strict quarantine rules having required travellers to isolate for up to 14 days upon their arrival in the country. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is having required travellers; use requiring travellers.

“Having required” shows an action completed before the main verb, but the rules require isolation now, at the same time as the extension. A present participle (or “that require”) expresses this.

Correct sentence: Qatar has extended strict quarantine rules requiring travellers to isolate for up to 14 days upon their arrival in the country.

question.en:
Spot the error in the below-given sentence.
"I wish I am taller than my brother". [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is I am; use I were (informally, “I was”).

After wish about a present situation that is not true, English uses the past subjunctive.

Correct sentence: I wish I were taller than my brother.
[काश मैं अपने भाई से लंबा होता।]

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
There isn't much time to spare. You'd better buy your ticket with the train. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The error is with the train; use on the train (or “for the train”).

A ticket is bought for a journey or on board a train; “with the train” expresses neither idea.

Correct sentence: There isn't much time to spare. You'd better buy your ticket on the train.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
The person with who Maya shared the flat had not paid his rent. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The error is who Maya shared the flat; use whom.

After a preposition (“with”), the relative pronoun takes the object form: with whom.

Correct sentence: The person with whom Maya shared the flat had not paid his rent.

question.en: Identify the incorrect sentence. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

1.en: Did they sent me any books for preparation of examination.

2.en: Reactions to the annual play have been favorable.

3.en: The author of the stories in these books is Mary Gomes.

4.en: Many lines in the poem are especially good.

solution.en:
Sentence 1 is incorrect: Did they sent should be Did they send.

After the auxiliary “did”, the main verb takes its base form. As a question, the sentence also needs a question mark.

Correct sentence: Did they send me any books for preparation of the examination?

The other sentences are grammatically correct.

question.en: Identify the incorrect sentence. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

1.en: All of the cities in California can to be affected by the rain yesterday.

2.en: Seven people were rescued from the fire yesterday.

3.en: Half of the boxes are empty as the children have eaten the chocolates.

4.en: Each packet can have a variable number of chocolates.

solution.en:
Sentence 1 is incorrect.

“Can” is followed by a bare infinitive (no “to”), and “can” cannot describe a past event such as “yesterday”.

Correct sentence: All of the cities in California may have been affected by the rain yesterday. (Or: …were affected by the rain yesterday.)

The other sentences are grammatically correct.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.
The child requested his mother to gave him a big chocolate because he had been very good all day long and deserved a treat. [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

1.en: The child requested his mother to

2.en: gave him a big chocolate because he

3.en: had been very good all day

solution.en:
The error is in part B: to gave should be to give.

The infinitive marker “to” is followed by the base form of the verb: requested his mother to give.

Correct sentence: The child requested his mother to give him a big chocolate because he had been very good all day long and deserved a treat.

question.en:
Find the incorrect part of the sentence:
He told to me about the incident. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: "Tell" takes a direct object without "to" (tell someone something). "Say" is the verb that takes "to" (say to someone).
So the error is in the part "to me".

Correct sentence:
He told me about the incident.

question.en:
Identify the part containing a grammatical or structural error:
Ten miles are a long distance to walk. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: A plural expression of distance, time, money or weight taken as one amount takes a singular verb.
"Ten miles" is a single distance, so "are" must be "is".

Correct sentence:
Ten miles is a long distance to walk.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The psychological bareness (1)/ of her narrative (2)/ precludes any embellishment, yet render (3)/ the structure more profoundly intimate. (4) [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: The subject "The psychological bareness" is singular, so both verbs joined by "yet" must be singular: "precludes … yet renders".
So the error is in part (3): "render" should be "renders".

Correct sentence:
The psychological bareness of her narrative precludes any embellishment, yet renders the structure more profoundly intimate.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The paradigm of rational choice theory (1)/ postulate that agents act consistently (2)/ to maximize utility, often ignoring (3)/ the constraints imposed by affective reasoning. (4) [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Rule: The subject is "The paradigm" (singular); "of rational choice theory" only describes it. A singular subject takes a singular verb.
So the error is in part (2): "postulate" should be "postulates".

Correct sentence:
The paradigm of rational choice theory postulates that agents act consistently to maximize utility, often ignoring the constraints imposed by affective reasoning.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
Can you borrow your book to me just for one day? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: Lend means to give something for a time; borrow means to take something for a time. When you ask someone to give you their book, the correct verb is lend ("lend something to someone").
So the error is in "borrow your".

Correct sentence:
Can you lend your book to me just for one day?

Related words: lend [उधार देना]; borrow [उधार लेना], as in "Can I borrow your book?"

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
Britains towns were given a new and elegant appearance between 1700 and 1830. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: Possession is shown with an apostrophe + s ('s). The towns belong to Britain, so "Britains towns" must be "Britain's towns".
So the error is in "Britains".

Correct sentence:
Britain's towns were given a new and elegant appearance between 1700 and 1830.

Note: when two adjectives describe the same noun, the article is used only once, as in "a new and elegant appearance".

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into three parts. Identify the part which contains a grammatical error (ignore any punctuation errors, if any). If there is no error in the sentence, then select 'No Error'.
(A) The investigation revealed that the culprit, / (B) rather than being remorseful, was insolent enough / (C) to have been taunted the victims during the trial. / (D) No Error [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

1.en: The investigation revealed that the culprit

2.en: rather than being remorseful, was insolent enough

3.en: to have been taunted the victims during the trial

solution.en:
Rule: "The victims" is the object of "taunt", so the active perfect infinitive (to have + V3) is needed. The passive "to have been taunted" cannot take an object here.
So the error is in part (C).

Correct sentence:
The investigation revealed that the culprit, rather than being remorseful, was insolent enough to have taunted the victims during the trial.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into three parts. Identify the part which contains a grammatical error (ignore any punctuation errors, if any). If there is no error in the sentence, then select 'No Error'.
(A) The strategy adopted by the administration / (B) is far superior than / (C) the one implemented by the previous committee. / (D) No Error [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

1.en: The strategy adopted by the administration

3.en: the one implemented by the previous committee

solution.en:
Rule: Superior is a Latin comparative and takes "to", not "than". "Far" correctly strengthens the comparison.
So the error is in part (B).

Correct sentence:
The strategy adopted by the administration is far superior to the one implemented by the previous committee.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
While the algorithm claims objectivity (1)/, it inadvertently reify bias (2)/ embedded in its training data, (3)/ perpetuating systemic inequities across demographics. (4) [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: A singular subject takes a singular verb in the simple present (verb + s/es).

The subject of part (2) is "it" (the algorithm), which is singular, so "reify" must be "reifies".
Reify [अमूर्त को मूर्त/वास्तविक रूप देना] means to make something abstract appear concrete or real.

Correct sentence:
While the algorithm claims objectivity, it inadvertently reifies bias embedded in its training data, perpetuating systemic inequities across demographics.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Much of the guidelines (1)/ pertaining to AI governance (2)/ were based on speculative models (3)/ and industry projections. (4) [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: Much is used with uncountable nouns; many is used with plural countable nouns.

"Guidelines" is a plural countable noun, so "Much of the guidelines" must be "Many of the guidelines". The plural verb "were" then agrees correctly.

Correct sentence:
Many of the guidelines pertaining to AI governance were based on speculative models and industry projections.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
What troubled the evaluators most (1)/ was not the complexity of the argument (2)/ but that its logic (3)/ and conclusions were fundamentally flawed. (4) [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: The correlative pair not … but … must join grammatically parallel elements.

Part (2) gives a noun phrase — "the complexity of the argument" — but part (3) begins a that-clause — "but that its logic …". This is faulty parallelism.
Part (3) should also begin with a noun phrase, e.g., "but the fact that its logic …".

Correct sentence:
What troubled the evaluators most was not the complexity of the argument but the fact that its logic and conclusions were fundamentally flawed.

question.en:
Spot the error in the below-given sentence.
"She can sings very well". [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 3]

solution.en:
Rule: A modal verb (can, could, may, must, will, shall …) is always followed by the base form of the verb.

"can sings" is wrong; it should be "can sing".

Correct sentence:
She can sing very well.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
The people here have nothing. Their poverty's extreme. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is poverty's; use poverty is.

Rule: The contraction 's after a noun is informal and can be read as a possessive (poverty's = of poverty). In a formal sentence, write the verb in full.

Correct sentence: The people here have nothing. Their poverty is extreme.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
The palace is heavily guarded, because inside it's walls sit the European leaders. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is inside it's walls; use inside its walls.

Rule: It's means "it is/it has". The possessive form of "it" is its (without an apostrophe).

Correct sentence: The palace is heavily guarded, because inside its walls sit the European leaders.

question.en: Identify the incorrect sentence. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: Mitali's hair is long and black.

2.en: Either of the alternatives seems to present major difficulties.

3.en: One of the cars in the garage is fifty years old.

4.en: Sharon has shared her devastating grief after the sudden death of her 57-year-old brother.

solution.en:
The sentence marked incorrect is "Either of the alternatives seems to present major difficulties."

Rule: Either means "one of two". When the number of choices is not limited to two, any of is used instead: "Any of the alternatives seems to present major difficulties."

Sentence 1 (hair takes a singular verb), sentence 3 (one of + plural noun + singular verb) and sentence 4 are correct.

question.en: Identify the incorrect sentence. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: Beautiful furniture make the house elegant and looks sophisticated at the same time.

2.en: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) is thousands of years old and has changed little over the centuries.

3.en: Folktales can be used to help children develop strong reading skills, study other cultures, and discover a love of stories.

4.en: Clothing is expensive because of the financial shakeup it received during the COVID-19 pandemic.

solution.en:
The incorrect sentence is "Beautiful furniture make the house elegant and looks sophisticated at the same time."

Rule: Furniture is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb: makes. The two actions must also be parallel.

Correct sentence: Beautiful furniture makes the house elegant and sophisticated at the same time.

The other three sentences are grammatically correct.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.
The ancient ruins attract thousands of tourists every year who are fascinating by the rich history and culture of the place. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

2.en: of tourists every year who are

solution.en:
The error is in part C: fascinating by should be fascinated by.

Rule: The past participle (fascinated) describes how a person feels; the -ing form describes the thing that causes the feeling.

Correct sentence: The ancient ruins attract thousands of tourists every year who are fascinated by the rich history and culture of the place.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Fewer of the experimental designs (1)/ was compatible with the theoretical model (2)/ proposed by the research team (3)/ in their meta-analysis. (4) [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Part (2) has the error: was should be were.

Rule: Fewer of + plural noun is plural (fewer is used with countable plural nouns), so the verb must be plural.

Correct sentence: Fewer of the experimental designs were compatible with the theoretical model proposed by the research team in their meta-analysis.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
We don't have to go to the party, don't we? We can stay at home. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The error is "don't we".

Rule: A negative statement takes a positive question tag. "We don't have to go" is negative, so the tag must be "do we?"

Correct sentence: We don't have to go to the party, do we? We can stay at home.

question.en:
The sentence below has errors in two parts which are highlighted in bold. Identify the same.
The reef is on risk of (A) losing its coveted World Heritage Status on occasion of (B) ocean warming, fuelled by (C) climate change, which is damaging its health(D). [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The errors are in parts A and B.

A: "on risk of" → at risk of (fixed phrase meaning "in danger of").
B: "on occasion of" → on account of / because of; a cause is needed here, while "on the occasion of" means "at the time of an event".

Correct sentence: The reef is at risk of losing its coveted World Heritage Status on account of ocean warming, fuelled by climate change, which is damaging its health.

Parts C and D are correct, so the answer is BA.

question.en:
Identify the error in the below-given sentence.
"The police has arrested the suspect in the case". [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The error is "has".

Rule: Police is a collective noun always used in the plural, so it takes have. (Similarly: cattle, people, clergy.)

Correct sentence: The police have arrested the suspect in the case.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.
The insightful documentary explored the profound impact of social media on mental health between young adults globally today. [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Part (3) has the error: between should be among.

Rule: Between is used for two persons or things; among is used for more than two or a group. "Young adults globally" is a large group.

Correct sentence: The insightful documentary explored the profound impact of social media on mental health among young adults globally today.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
The news that the plane had crashed will be coming as a terrible shock. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error lies in part 3: will be coming.

Rule & Explanation: The future continuous tense ('will be coming') expresses an action in progress at a specific time in the future. However, receiving news and experiencing emotional shock occurs as a punctual event, not a continuous process. When stating the predictable effect of dramatic news, English uses the simple future: 'will come as a terrible shock' (or 'came as a terrible shock').

Correct sentence: The news that the plane had crashed will come as a terrible shock.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
The bank will be continued to transfer the interest to your account unless instructed otherwise. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error lies in part 2: will be continued.

Rule & Explanation: The subject 'The bank' is the active agent performing the action of transferring interest, not the recipient of the action. The passive construction 'will be continued to transfer' is grammatically incorrect. The verb must be in the active voice: 'will continue to transfer'.

Correct sentence: The bank will continue to transfer the interest to your account unless instructed otherwise.

question.en: Identify the incorrect sentence. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

1.en: She has got cold and cough.

2.en: Only a few people came to the party.

3.en: Could you lend me some of your books today?

4.en: He has more sense than you have.

solution.en:
The incorrect sentence is Option 1.

Rule & Explanation: In standard English idiom, the illnesses 'cold' and 'cough' are singular countable nouns that require indefinite articles: one catches or suffers from 'a cold' and 'a cough'. Thus, the correct idiomatic expression is 'She has got a cold and a cough'.
• Option 2 correctly uses 'a few' with countable 'people'.
• Option 3 correctly uses 'some' in a polite request expected to elicit an affirmative response.
• Option 4 correctly uses the comparative 'more sense than'.

question.en:
Identify the error in the below-given sentence.
"The government have decided to increase taxes". [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The error is in have (Option 2).

Rule: In standard grammar (especially in standardized examination syntax), collective nouns like 'government', 'committee', or 'jury' acting as a unified singular entity take a singular verb ('has decided').

Correct sentence: The government has decided to increase taxes.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.
The antique grandfather clock in the hallway have not worked properly for over a decade now, which is a real shame for the family. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

3.en: properly for over a decade now,

4.en: which is a real shame for the family.

solution.en:
The error is in part 2: the hallway have not worked.

Subject-Verb Agreement Rule:
• Identify the true grammatical subject: 'The antique grandfather clock' (singular noun).
• The prepositional phrase 'in the hallway' simply modifies the clock and does not affect grammatical number.
• A singular subject takes the singular auxiliary verb has, not 'have'.

Correct sentence: The antique grandfather clock in the hallway has not worked properly for over a decade now...

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
He was imprisoned for many years, without many occasions, in both South Africa and India. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Error: “without many occasions” gives no sense. The intended idea is that he was jailed repeatedly, which is expressed as “on many occasions”.
Correct sentence: He was imprisoned for many years, on many occasions, in both South Africa and India.
“imprisoned for”, “many years” and “in both” are used correctly.

Therefore, without many occasions.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
The village is very isolated, their being no bus service. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Error: “their” is a possessive pronoun (their house). The sentence needs the adverb “there” in the absolute phrase “there being no bus service”.
Correct sentence: The village is very isolated, there being no bus service.
The other parts are grammatically correct.

Therefore, their being.

question.en:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.
It is a fact that there are most cars in Los Angeles than people. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Error: “most” is a superlative and cannot be followed by “than”. A comparison between cars and people needs the comparative “more”.
Correct sentence: It is a fact that there are more cars in Los Angeles than people.
“than people”, “a fact that” and “It is a fact” are correct.

Therefore, most cars.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.
Please provide a detailing explanation of the research methodology used in your recent scientific paper for clarification purposes requested by the board. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

2.en: of the research methodology used in

4.en: clarification purposes requested by the board.

solution.en:
Error: A noun (explanation) must be described by an adjective. “Detailing” is a verb form; the adjective is “detailed”.
Correct: Please provide a detailed explanation …
The other parts are correct.

Therefore, Please provide a detailing explanation.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts, namely A, B, C and D, which are given in the alternatives. Select the alternative that contains the part of the sentence with an error.
Remember to brush your teeth thorough before you go to bed every single night without fail as instructed by the dentist. [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

2.en: thorough before you go to bed

solution.en:
Error: “brush” is a verb, so it must be modified by an adverb. “Thorough” is an adjective; the adverb is “thoroughly”.
Correct: Remember to brush your teeth thoroughly before you go to bed …
The other parts are correct.

Therefore, thorough before you go to bed.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into three parts. Identify the part which contains a grammatical error (ignore any punctuation errors, if any). If there is no error in the sentence, then select 'No Error'.
(A) Little did the CEO realise that the proposed restructuring / (B) would be met with such vehemence by the labour unions / (C) as to force a complete abandonment of the project. / (D) No Error [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

1.en: Little did the CEO realise that the proposed restructuring

2.en: would be met with such vehemence by the labour unions

3.en: as to force a complete abandonment of the project

solution.en:
Check each part
(A) “Little did the CEO realise …” – correct inversion after the negative adverb “little” (auxiliary “did” + subject + base verb).
(B) “would be met with such vehemence …” – correct passive with “would”.
(C) “as to force …” – correct, because “such … as to” expresses a result.
All parts are correct, so there is no error.

Therefore, No error.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
In Woolf's imaginary legacy (1)/, the room functions not just as sanctuary (2)/ but also as a discursive axis (3)/ where womanhood collapse into multiplicity. (4) [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** The subject **womanhood** is an uncountable singular noun and requires a singular verb (**collapses**) in the present simple tense.
**Correction:** "...where womanhood **collapses** into multiplicity."
Parts (1), (2), and (3) are grammatically sound.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Despite its ostensible neutrality (1)/, the bureaucratic apparatus (2)/ enact normative controls (3)/ that homogenize diverse expressions of identity. (4) [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** The subject **apparatus** is singular in this context and requires the singular present verb form **enacts**.
**Correction:** "...the bureaucratic apparatus **enacts** normative controls..."
The remaining clauses are constructed correctly.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
Within postcolonial discourse (1)/, hybridity operate not as a passive amalgamation (2)/ but as a site of contestation (3)/ and negotiated subjectivity. (4) [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** The abstract noun **hybridity** is singular and must take the singular verb form **operates**.
**Correction:** "...hybridity **operates** not as a passive amalgamation..."
Parts (1), (3), and (4) contain no grammatical errors.

question.en:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.
The researcher who the panel had nominated (1)/ for the ethics award (2)/ were present at the plenary session (3)/ but declined to speak. (4) [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Rule:** The head subject of the sentence is the singular noun **The researcher**, which demands the singular past verb **was** rather than the plural **were**.

question.en:
Read the passage and answer the question:
Sleep is a vital biological process that restores the body and mind. However, for millions of people worldwide, this natural rhythm is disrupted by sleep disorders. These conditions can range from insomnia, where (4) person struggles to fall or stay asleep, to sleep apnea, a potentially serious condition where breathing repeatedly stops and starts during sleep.
Chronic sleep problems (3) have far-reaching consequences. They impair concentration, weaken the immune system, and increase the risk of conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, and depression. The cumulative effect of poor sleep over time can be as harmful as a poor diet or lack of exercise.
Causes of sleep disorders vary (5). Stress, irregular schedules, excessive screen time before bed, and underlying medical conditions are common triggers. Modern lifestyles, with their relentless pace and constant connectivity, have only worsened the problem.
Treatment depends on the underlying cause. For some, improving (1) sleep hygiene such as maintaining a regular sleep schedule, limiting caffeine, and creating a calm bedtime routine can make a significant difference. In more severe cases, medical intervention or therapy may be necessary.
Ultimately, addressing sleep disorders is not just about avoiding fatigue; it's about protecting overall health and ensuring that the body's (2) restorative processes function as they should.

Question: The word "restorative" in the passage is closest in meaning to: [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Restorative [पुनः स्वस्थ करने वाला, नवीनीकरण करने वाला] means able to bring back health, strength or freshness. The passage says sleep “restores the body and mind”, so the body’s restorative processes are its healing or renewing processes.

[नींद के दौरान शरीर की वे प्रक्रियाएँ जो थकान दूर करके उसे फिर से स्वस्थ और तरोताज़ा करती हैं।]

Damaging — causing harm [हानिकारक]
Healing or renewing — making healthy or fresh again [उपचार या नवीनीकरण करने वाला]
Weakening — making weaker [कमज़ोर करने वाला]
Boring — dull [उबाऊ]

Simple alternatives for restorative here: refreshing, rejuvenating, curative.

question.en: Based on the cloze passage on sleep disorders, the phrase "sleep hygiene" most nearly means: [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

2.en: Sleeping in a clean room only

3.en: Habits and practices that promote good quality sleep

The passage explains sleep hygiene through its examples: a regular sleep schedule, limiting caffeine and a calm bedtime routine. So it means habits and practices that promote good-quality sleep.

[अच्छी नींद के लिए अपनाई जाने वाली अच्छी आदतें और दिनचर्या।]

“Hygiene” is used figuratively here; it is not about cleaning the bed or the room, and medical treatment is mentioned separately for severe cases.

Should — duty or advice [चाहिए]
Might — a weak, uncertain possibility [शायद]
Will — certainty about the future [निश्चित रूप से होगा]
Can — general possibility or ability [सकता है]

The next sentences state the effects as known facts, so the general-possibility modal fits best.

Swimming is one of the most popular recreational and competitive activities worldwide, valued for both its fitness benefits and its ability to provide relaxation. Unlike many forms of exercise, swimming is (1) low-impact, making it ideal for people of all ages and fitness levels. The buoyancy of water supports the body, reducing strain on joints while still (3) resistance to build muscle strength and endurance.
Beyond its physical advantages, swimming is also a valuable life skill. Knowing how to swim can be (2) "life-saving" in emergencies and helps individuals enjoy other water-based activities such as boating, diving, and surfing. Competitive swimming, on the other hand, demands rigorous training, discipline, and excellent technique.
Different strokes-freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, and butterfly-engage various muscle groups and require distinct breathing patterns. Regular swimming improves cardiovascular health, increases lung capacity, and promotes overall well-being. It's also an effective way to reduce stress, as the rhythmic movements and sensation of being in water can have a calming effect on the mind.
However, safety is crucial. Swimmers should always be aware of (4) environment, whether in pools, lakes, or the ocean, and follow proper safety guidelines. Learning under supervision (5) using appropriate gear ensures a safe and enjoyable experience.

Question: In the passage, what does "low-impact" most nearly mean? [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

2.en: Causing minimal stress or strain on the body

solution.en:
Low-impact [शरीर पर कम दबाव डालने वाला] describes exercise that puts little stress on the joints and bones. The passage adds that buoyancy reduces strain on joints, so it means causing minimal stress or strain on the body.

[तैराकी में जोड़ों पर बहुत कम दबाव पड़ता है।]

It does not mean ineffective or boring: the same passage says swimming builds strength and endurance.

[आपात स्थिति में तैरना आना किसी की जान बचा सकता है।]

The other options — earning money, enjoyment and appearance — have nothing to do with emergencies.

question.en:

solution.en:
Use their.

The subject “swimmers” is plural and third person, so the matching possessive is “their”.

question.en:
In the given passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage intently and choose the most appropriate option to fill in each blank:

Education is usually seen as the pillar of a successful society. It provides people with the necessary information and skills to advance their lives and serve their communities. Apart from studies, education develops critical thinking and (1)______ making people analyse issues and make sound decisions.
One of the difficulties with education today is achieving equal access for everyone. Socioeconomic inequality tends to form obstacles, leaving disadvantaged groups lacking resources. To address this, investment must be made in infrastructure and (2)______ policies that are focused on inclusivity.
Technology has also revolutionized education, and learning has become more accessible with the help of online platforms. This change brings concerns regarding the (3)______ of typical classroom experiences, which focus on direct interaction and collaboration.
Finally, learning is not simply the process of gaining knowledge; it's about the molding of values and instilling a sense of (4)______ and (5)______.
By giving equal weight to academic success and social responsibility, societies can build a future that is both innovative and (5)______.

What should come in the place of blank number 1? [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Creativity [रचनात्मकता] completes the pair of thinking skills that education develops along with critical thinking: thinking critically and creatively helps people analyse issues from fresh angles and make sound decisions.

[शिक्षा आलोचनात्मक सोच के साथ रचनात्मकता भी विकसित करती है, जिससे लोग मुद्दों का विश्लेषण कर सही निर्णय ले पाते हैं।]

Memory — the ability to retain and recall information [स्मरण-शक्ति]; merely recalling facts does not by itself make people analyse issues
Creativity — the ability to produce new ideas [रचनात्मकता]
Physical strength — bodily power [शारीरिक शक्ति]
Athletic ability — skill in sports [खेल-कौशल]

“Critical thinking and creativity” is the natural pair of mental skills; physical strength and athletic ability have nothing to do with analysing issues.

Profitable — yielding financial gain [लाभदायक]
Chaotic — completely disordered [अव्यवस्थित]

Social responsibility points to long-term well-being, so “sustainable” is the word that pairs with “innovative”.

In the following question, some of the words in the passage have been left out. Read the passage carefully and choose the correct answer to each question out of the four alternatives and fill in the blanks.

Graphic novels have revolutionised modern storytelling by combining the power of words with visual art. Unlike traditional text-only books, they tell a complete story using comic-strip formats, illustrations, and dialogue bubbles. This unique blend makes reading highly engaging and easier to understand, especially for students who find long blocks of text (1)______. It also helps capture their attention for longer than text-only books do. Graphic novels gained popularity because of their ability to (2)______ rather than just tell. A single drawing can instantly express deep emotions, set a mysterious mood, or showcase a complex action scene that might otherwise take pages to describe. This dual format activates different parts of the brain simultaneously, improving visual literacy and memory retention. This also helps enhance creative (3)______ among students reading them and their ability to interpret context very well. Furthermore, graphic novels are not just for children; they tackle serious, mature themes like history, mental health, and social justice. They provide a voice to diverse perspectives, making complex global issues accessible to everyone. By weaving fine art with literature, graphic novels have proven that images can be just as powerful as written words in creating a deep, lasting (4)______ impact on (5)______.

What should come in blank 1? [Steno 09 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Intimidating [डराने वाला, भयभीत करने वाला] fits: some students find long blocks of text daunting, which is why graphic novels make reading easier for them.

[कुछ छात्रों को लंबे-लंबे पाठ-अंश डरावने/कठिन लगते हैं।]

Intimidating — frightening or overwhelming [भयभीत करने वाला]
Exciting — causing eager enthusiasm [रोमांचक]
Interesting — holding attention [रोचक]
Transforming — changing completely [रूपांतरित करने वाला]

Only a negative feeling explains why these students need an easier format.

In the given passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage intently and choose the most appropriate option to fill in each blank:

In a time characterized by deep ideological divides and epistemic uncertainty, the role of intellectuals has become increasingly (1)______. No longer confined to the ivory towers of academia, public thinkers are now thrust into digital arenas, where their ideas are subjected to the volatile currents of public sentiment and algorithmic amplification. This (2)______ from cloistered contemplation to performative intellectualism has raised concerns about the erosion of nuanced debate in favor of ideological branding.

The commodification of knowledge production, particularly within neoliberal structures, has reoriented scholarship toward metrics of visibility rather than depth. Consequently, the pursuit of truth is often (3)______ by the need for marketability, leaving complex ideas diluted to conform to audience expectations. Amid this shift, academic institutions themselves have become entangled in bureaucratic inertia, frequently adopting managerial logics that prioritize efficiency over (4)______.

To counter this drift, there must be a recommitment to critical inquiry as a mode of civic responsibility. Intellectual labor must resist assimilation into spectacle and instead cultivate spaces for deliberation that are both inclusive and rigorous. Only by embracing such an ethic of care can the academy preserve its (5)______ in shaping public reason.

Q1: What should come in the place of blank number 1? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Contested [विवादित] fits blank 1. The passage begins with "deep ideological divides and epistemic uncertainty", so the role of intellectuals has become a matter of dispute.

Option meanings
Unequivocal — clear, leaving no doubt [असंदिग्ध]
Contested — disputed, argued over [विवादित]
Triumphant — victorious [विजयी]
Peripheral — of minor importance, on the edge [गौण, परिधीय]

In a time characterized by deep ideological divides and epistemic uncertainty, the role of intellectuals has become increasingly (1)______. No longer confined to the ivory towers of academia, public thinkers are now thrust into digital arenas, where their ideas are subjected to the volatile currents of public sentiment and algorithmic amplification. This (2)______ from cloistered contemplation to performative intellectualism has raised concerns about the erosion of nuanced debate in favor of ideological branding.

The commodification of knowledge production, particularly within neoliberal structures, has reoriented scholarship toward metrics of visibility rather than depth. Consequently, the pursuit of truth is often (3)______ by the need for marketability, leaving complex ideas diluted to conform to audience expectations. Amid this shift, academic institutions themselves have become entangled in bureaucratic inertia, frequently adopting managerial logics that prioritize efficiency over (4)______.

To counter this drift, there must be a recommitment to critical inquiry as a mode of civic responsibility. Intellectual labor must resist assimilation into spectacle and instead cultivate spaces for deliberation that are both inclusive and rigorous. Only by embracing such an ethic of care can the academy preserve its (5)______ in shaping public reason.

Q5: What should come in the place of blank number 5? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Credence [विश्वसनीयता, मान्यता] fits blank 5. The passage worries that the academy is losing trust through spectacle and ideological branding. By embracing an ethic of care, it can preserve its credibility in shaping public reason.
"Primacy" does not fit, because the passage itself says intellectuals are no longer confined to academia, so the academy's first place is already gone; what can still be preserved is its credibility.

Option meanings
Credence — belief, trust, credibility [विश्वसनीयता]
Ubiquity — being present everywhere [सर्वव्यापकता]
Primacy — the state of being most important [प्रधानता]
Relatable — easy to identify with [जुड़ाव योग्य] (an adjective, so it cannot follow "its")

Records [अभिलेख] fits blank 1. The whole passage is about digitising land records, and blockchain is used to prevent tampering with records.

Boundaries — lines marking the limits of an area [सीमाएँ]

question.en:
In the given passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage intently and choose the most appropriate option to fill in each blank:

A plethora of cognitive and affective factors shape the intricate process of human decision-making. Even though we often believe that our choices are rationalized entirely, studies have shown that heuristics—or implicit bias and mental shortcuts—play a significant role. For example, the (1)________ effect leads people to put great weight on the first bit of information they gather, even if it is irrelevant. This can mislead judgment and result in faulty conclusions.

Another usual bias is (2)________, in which individuals search for information that validates their current assumptions while overlooking opposing evidence. This trend perpetuates stereotypes and might inhibit critical thinking. Emotional states also influence choices; an anxious person might become more cautious, while someone who is euphoric might take (3)________ risks.

In addition, social pressures must not be ignored. The need to follow group norms, referred to as (4)________, can cause people to make decisions they would not otherwise make. This is particularly clear in high-stress situations such as corporate boardrooms or political campaigns.

Knowing these psychological processes is critical to enhancing decision-making. Through increased awareness of our own biases and the ability to challenge our assumptions, we can make more (5)________ decisions that balance logic with empathy.

What should come in the place of blank number 1? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Anchoring [आरंभिक जानकारी पर अत्यधिक निर्भरता] fits: the anchoring effect is the tendency to rely too heavily on the first piece of information received.
The passage says the effect "leads people to put great weight on the first bit of information they gather, even if it is irrelevant".

Option meanings
Anchoring — over-reliance on the first information received [प्रथम सूचना पर टिक जाना]
Confirmation bias — seeking only information that supports one's beliefs [पुष्टि पूर्वाग्रह]
Availability bias — judging by examples that come easily to mind [उपलब्धता पूर्वाग्रह]
Overconfidence bias — overestimating one's own ability or knowledge [अति-आत्मविश्वास पूर्वाग्रह]

question.en:
Read the cloze passage and answer the following questions:

Millets, a group of small-seeded grains, ______(3) for thousands of years in India and other parts of Asia and Africa. Once considered the “poor man’s food,” they are now gaining recognition for their (1) nutritional value and environmental benefits. Rich in fibre, protein, vitamins, and minerals, millets are a powerhouse of health, aiding digestion, improving heart health, and helping regulate blood sugar levels.

Unlike rice and wheat, millets require far less water to grow and can thrive in arid and semi-arid regions. This makes them not only a healthy choice but also a (2) sustainable one, particularly important in the face of climate change and depleting water resources.

There are _____(4) varieties of millets, including finger millet (ragi), pearl millet (bajra), and foxtail millet, each with its unique taste and health benefits. These grains can be used in a wide range of dishes from traditional rotis and porridges to modern snacks and desserts.

Despite their benefits, millets had fallen out of favour for decades due to changing food preferences and the dominance of rice and wheat in markets. However, with increasing health awareness ______(5) government campaigns, they are making a comeback on urban menus and in packaged food products.

In the passage, what does “nutritional” most nearly mean? [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

3.en: Related to value of food for health

solution.en:
Nutritional [पोषण संबंधी] means relating to the value of food for health and growth.
The passage supports this: millets are "rich in fibre, protein, vitamins, and minerals" and "a powerhouse of health".

Option meanings
Related to flavor — about taste [स्वाद से संबंधित]
Related to cooking speed — about how fast food cooks [पकने की गति से संबंधित]
Related to value of food for health — nutritional [पोषण संबंधी]
Related to farming — agricultural [कृषि संबंधी]

Once considered the “poor man’s food,” they are now gaining recognition for their (1) nutritional value and environmental benefits. Rich in fibre, protein, vitamins, and minerals, millets are a powerhouse of health, aiding digestion, improving heart health, and helping regulate blood sugar levels.

Despite their benefits, millets had fallen out of favour for decades due to changing food preferences and the dominance of rice and wheat in markets. However, with increasing health awareness ______(5) government campaigns, they are making a comeback on urban menus and in packaged food products.

Choose the correct auxiliary verb and main verb: (3) [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Rule: An action that began in the past and continues up to now, with "for thousands of years", takes the present perfect. The subject "Millets" is plural and the grains are grown by people, so the passive have been + V3 is needed.

Correct sentence:
Millets, a group of small-seeded grains, have been cultivated for thousands of years in India and other parts of Asia and Africa.

"Has been cultivated" is singular, "Having cultivated" is not a finite verb, and "Had cultivated" is active and places the action entirely in the past.

question.en:
The theory of evolution, first systematically articulated by Charles Darwin, provides a comprehensive explanation for how species gradually change and diversify over time through the process of natural selection. Organisms possessing traits that are better adapted to their specific environments are more likely to survive, reproduce successfully and pass these advantageous traits on to subsequent generations. Over extended periods, minor variations accumulate, leading to remarkable adaptations and the emergence of entirely new species. Extensive evidence supporting evolutionary theory comes from the fossil record, comparative anatomy and modern genetic studies. Evolutionary principles illuminate the vast diversity of life, the intricate relationships among organisms and the development of complex biological traits. Although initially controversial, the concept of evolution is now widely accepted within the scientific community and serves as a foundational framework in biology, medicine and ecology. Understanding evolution enables humans to fully appreciate the profound interconnectedness of life and the natural mechanisms driving ongoing biological change.

The theory of evolution explains how species change over ______. [Steno 10 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
The passage states that the theory explains "how species gradually change and diversify over time through the process of natural selection".
Evolution is a slow process spread over long periods, not minutes, hours or days.

Maintains — keeps going [बनाए रखता है]

Amplifies and maintains give the opposite meaning.

Straightforward — simple and clear [सरल]

Arduous [कठिन, श्रमसाध्य] means difficult and requiring great effort. The passage supports this: writers spend "countless hours drafting, revising, and battling self-doubt".

Read the cloze passage and answer the following questions:

Journalism is often called the fourth pillar of democracy, alongside the legislature, executive, and judiciary. Its primary role is to inform the public, (1) scrutinize those in power, and ensure that citizens can make informed decisions. A free and responsible press serves as a watchdog, exposing corruption, amplifying marginalized voices, and holding institutions accountable.

However, this role is neither simple nor without challenges. Journalists frequently operate under intense pressure, balancing the need for (2) objectivity with the realities of deadlines, editorial bias, and, in some cases, censorship. In countries with restricted press freedom, the pursuit of truth can even put reporters' lives at risk.

The rise of digital media has transformed (3), making information more accessible but also creating new problems like misinformation and "fake news." In such an environment, the credibility of journalists depends heavily on rigorous fact-checking and ethical reporting standards.

A vibrant and independent press (4) essential to the health of any democracy. Without it, power can go unchecked, public debate may wither, and citizens risk being left in the dark. Journalism is not merely a profession; it is a civic responsibility that (5) the very foundation of democratic life.

The word "scrutinize" in the passage is closest in meaning to: [Steno 11 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Scrutinize [बारीकी से जाँचना] means to examine closely; the press closely examines the actions of those in power.

Option meanings
Ignore — pay no attention [अनदेखा करना]
Announce publicly — declare openly [सार्वजनिक घोषणा करना]
Approve quickly — sanction at once [शीघ्र स्वीकृति देना]
Examine closely — correct [बारीकी से जाँचना]

Related words: Scrutinize: inspect, probe, analyse.

Select the correct verb form for blank (3) in the cloze passage:
"South India, known for its tropical climate, (3) heavy rainfall during both the southwest and northeast monsoons." [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Subject-Verb Agreement Rule:
• The subject is the singular geographical proper noun 'South India' (the appositive phrase 'known for its tropical climate' is set off by commas and does not change the subject number).
• A singular subject in the simple present tense (stating a recurring climatic fact) requires a third-person singular verb ending in -s: experiences.

Complete sentence: South India, known for its tropical climate, experiences heavy rainfall...

question.en:
Identify which pronoun is correct for blank (4) in the cloze passage:
"Rural areas face (4) own challenges, with farmlands getting inundated..." [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Pronoun-Antecedent Agreement:
• The antecedent is the plural noun phrase 'Rural areas'.
• The third-person plural possessive determiner referring to plural inanimate/geographic entities is their.
• 'His' and 'her' are gendered singular pronouns; 'its' is neuter singular.

Complete sentence: Rural areas face their own challenges...

question.en:
Choose the appropriate word to complete the sentence for blank (5) in the cloze passage:
"Effective urban planning, investment in drainage infrastructure, and community awareness are (5) to mitigating the impact of these events." [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Grammatical Category Rule:
• In the predicate construction 'Subject + linking verb (are) + Predicate Adjective + prepositional phrase', a predicate adjective is required to describe the compound subject.
• Crucial [अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण, अनिवार्य] is the adjective.
• 'Crucially' is an adverb, while 'cruciality' and 'crucialness' are awkward noun forms.

Complete sentence: ...community awareness are crucial to mitigating the impact of these events.

The phrase "state of deep tranquility" most nearly means: [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:

Option meanings
• Moment of excitement — a period of high emotional arousal [उत्तेजना का क्षण]
• Period of extreme calmness — a state of profound peace and serenity [गहरी शांति की अवस्था]
• Phase of confusion — a period of perplexity or disorientation [भ्रम की स्थिति]
• Feeling of tiredness — physical exhaustion or fatigue [थकान की भावना]

solution.en:
Cognitive [संज्ञानात्मक, विचार संबंधी] (derived from Latin cognoscere 'to know') is an adjective pertaining to the mental processes of perception, memory, reasoning, comprehension, and intellect. Hence, it is closest to 'Related to thinking and understanding'.

Related words: intellectual, mental, rational, conceptual.

Identify which verb is correct to complete the sentence for blank (3) in the cloze passage:
"Meditation is an ancient practice that (3) mental clarity, emotional stability, and overall well-being." [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Contextual Vocabulary & Agreement:
• The singular antecedent 'an ancient practice' is the subject of the relative clause introduced by 'that', requiring a third-person singular verb.
• Contextually, meditation enhances and encourages positive mental clarity and well-being. The verb meaning to support, encourage, or foster is promotes [बढ़ावा देता है].
• 'Disrupts' (disturbs), 'neglects' (ignores), and 'diminishes' (reduces) express negative meanings contrary to the passage.

Complete sentence: Meditation is an ancient practice that promotes mental clarity...

question.en:
Choose the correct modal verb for blank (4) in the cloze passage:
"However, developing a consistent meditation habit (4) be challenging." [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Modal of Theoretical Possibility:
• The modal verb can is used to express general, theoretical possibility or potential difficulty (can be challenging) [चुनौतीपूर्ण हो सकता है].
• 'Must' expresses necessity or deduction; 'should' expresses duty or advice; 'will' asserts absolute certainty, which is too rigid.

Complete sentence: However, developing a consistent meditation habit can be challenging.

solution.en:
Participial Clause Rule:
• The sentence contains a complete main clause ('It bridges...'). A comma following a complete clause introducing a consequential result requires a present participle (-ing form) functioning as a non-finite result clause: making it a timeless tool.
• Finite forms like 'makes' or 'made' create a comma splice.

Complete sentence: ...needs, making it a timeless tool for inner peace...

question.en:
In the following question, some of the words in the passage have been left out. Read the passage carefully and choose the correct answer to each question out of the four alternatives and fill in the blanks.

The REM (Rapid Eye Movement) cycle is a sleep stage (1)______ by rapid eye movements, low muscle tone throughout the body, and vivid dreaming. It is a deeply fascinating stage of our sleep that plays a (2)______ role in brain development and mental health. During a normal night, our body cycles through different sleep stages every ninety minutes. REM sleep is the final stage of this cycle, occurring mostly in the early morning hours. It gets its name because our eyes rapidly dart back and forth behind our closed eyelids, signalling (3)______ brain activity. To protect us from physically acting out these wild dreams and hurting ourselves, our brain temporarily (4)______ our major muscles. This temporary lockdown is called muscle atonia. Neurologists view the REM cycle as the brain's ultimate overnight cleanup crew; it (5)______ our daily emotions, sharpens our memory, and stores everything we learned during the day.

What should come in blank 1? [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Blank 1: “a sleep stage ______ by rapid eye movements, low muscle tone … and vivid dreaming.”
The features listed are what mark or define this stage – “characterised by”.
Simplified, Criticised and Threatened do not fit “a stage … by its features”.

Therefore, Characterised.

Sowa-Rigpa, literally means the "Knowledge of Healing". It is one of the world's oldest and best-documented traditional medical systems, (1)______ practised in Tibet and the Himalayan regions of India, Bhutan, Nepal, and Mongolia. Its practitioners are traditionally known as Amchis. Similar to Ayurveda, Sowa-Rigpa is built on the (2)______ that everything in the universe, including the human body, is made of five basic elements: Earth, Water, Fire, Wind, and Space. In the body, these elements form three primary internal energies that (3)______ respiration, metabolism, and fluid balance. When these energies are perfectly balanced, a person enjoys good health; an (4)______ caused by a bad diet, stress, or seasonal changes leads to illness. To diagnose diseases, Amchis use highly (5)______ non-invasive methods such as checking a patient's pulse and analysing urine.

What should come in blank 1? [Steno 12 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Blank 1: “one of the world's oldest … medical systems, ______ practised in Tibet and the Himalayan regions …”
The regions listed are where the system is mainly followed – “primarily practised”.
Rarely, Accidentally and Secretly contradict its status as a well-documented, established system.

Therefore, Primarily.

question.en:
The architecture of modern policymaking increasingly reflects a shift from dialogic consensus to technocratic unilateralism. Public consultation, once a hallmark of democratic ethos, is now frequently (1) ______ by algorithmic forecasting and data-driven mandates. While such models brag precision, they risk sustaining systemic (2) ______ by embedding pre-existing prejudices into ostensibly neutral code. This evolution is further complicated by the political spectacle, where performative symbolism often supplants substantive reform. Leaders indulge in rhetorical grandstanding, constructing narratives that are (3) ______ rather than transformative. Consequently, public trust erodes, not due to apathy but from acute (4) ______ -a recognition that participation no longer guarantees influence. To reclaim legitimacy, institutions must reimagine governance not as a procedural mechanism but as an iterative, dialogical act. This demands epistemic humility, the willingness to engage multiple worldviews without defaulting to technocratic (5) ______. Only then can policy transcend compliance and cultivate authentic democratic agency.
Q1: What should come in the place of blank number 1? [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
**Superseded** means replaced or supplanted by something newer.
The passage contrasts traditional democratic consultation with modern unilateral data mechanisms that replace it.
Options (b), (c), and (d) do not convey complete technological replacement.

question.en: [Refer to the passage in Q.178] Q2: What should come in the place of blank number 2? [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The subsequent phrase "embedding pre-existing prejudices into ostensibly neutral code" indicates that systemic **biases** are what algorithms risk perpetuating.
Options (a), (b), and (d) do not denote systematic historical prejudice.

question.en: [Refer to the passage in Q.178] Q3: What should come in the place of blank number 3? [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The context of "performative symbolism" and "rhetorical grandstanding" rather than real reform points to narratives that are merely decorative and superficial (**Ornamental**).
**Sagacious**, **Strategic**, and **Iterative** describe purposeful or wise actions, contradicting the author's critique.

question.en: [Refer to the passage in Q.178] Q4: What should come in the place of blank number 4? [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The passage clarifies that trust erodes "not due to apathy but from acute [feeling]" when citizens realize participation has no influence, which defines **Disillusionment** (loss of faith/disenchantment).
Options (a), (c), and (d) fail to align with the dashed explanation in the sentence.

question.en: [Refer to the passage in Q.178] Q5: What should come in the place of blank number 5? [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
In contrast to "epistemic humility" and openness to other worldviews, an inflexible adherence to technical arrogance is called technocratic **Dogmatism**.
Options (a), (b), and (d) do not contrast logically with epistemic humility.

question.en:
Contemporary governance will typically disguise itself in terms of agility and crisis response. From climate early warning systems to pandemic dashboards, there is a rapidly increasing apparatus that promises the vision of being in control. Such aids, while useful, tend to (1) ______ the public eye away from structural disparities by concentrating on short-term metrics. What looks like responsiveness tends to be mere reactivity in a system that is optimized for optics, not results. Governments implement short-term programs, presented as "emergency relief," but too frequently without vision or representation in the long term. These measures are hailed not for their depth but for their urgency. The theatrics of governance are most visible, while the slow violence of underfinance of healthcare, food insecurity, and housing abandonment goes on and on. Policymaking is performative in this environment and is not evaluated by what it achieves but by how visible it is. The outcome is an administration style that (2) ______ true change by replacing announcements with action. This is particularly true in the way that disasters are framed. The media cycle dramatizes, politicians act out urgency, and citizen complaints are quantified into abstraction. Gradually, this storytelling method (3) ______ distress into consumable portions reducing complexity for dissemination. Crisis is a stage; the state, its actor. To meet this, we need to question how emergencies are constructed, not merely how they are governed. Otherwise, the instruments we construct to deal with suffering risk inadvertently (4) ______ it, locking people in situations they are assured are being rectified. Resilience, without responsibility, is a code for abandonment. Unless governance examines its own aesthetics, it will be a simulation everywhere, but (5) ______ where it is needed most.
Q1: What should come in the place of blank number 1? [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The collocation **divert ... away from** means to distract or redirect attention elsewhere.
The dashboards draw attention away from structural deep-rooted inequalities.
Options (b), (c), and (d) do not match the construction with "away from".

question.en: [Refer to the passage in Q.183] Q2: What should come in the place of blank number 2? [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The text states that administration replaces substantive action with announcements, producing a mere appearance of progress; thus it **simulates** true change (echoing "it will be a simulation everywhere" later in the passage).
Options (b), (c), and (d) fail to maintain the passage's central theme of performative simulation.

question.en: [Refer to the passage in Q.183] Q3: What should come in the place of blank number 3? [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
Turning widespread distress into discrete, disconnected "consumable portions" means breaking it down or dividing it into pieces (**fragments**).
**Filters**, **distills**, and **translates** do not capture the compartmentalizing effect described in the text.

question.en: [Refer to the passage in Q.183] Q4: What should come in the place of blank number 4? [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
By "locking people in situations they are assured are being rectified," the instruments perpetuate or lengthen the suffering; thus they risk **prolonging** it.
Options (a), (c), and (d) do not align with the phrase "locking people in situations."

question.en: [Refer to the passage in Q.183] Q5: What should come in the place of blank number 5? [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

solution.en:
The contrast is between governance being "a simulation everywhere" (superficially visible) but fundamentally missing or **absent** where genuine assistance is most critical.
Options (a), (b), and (d) run contrary to the critical tone established by the author.

question.en:
In the given passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage intently and choose the most appropriate option to fill in each blank:

As post-industrial societies gravitate towards algorithmic governance, the contours of democratic deliberation are being steadily (1)______. What was once a domain of slow-paced, participatory engagement has now been supplanted by platforms that privilege immediacy and spectacle. The metrics of influence-likes, shares, and impressions-act as a surrogate for rational consensus, creating a new epistemic environment where the distinction between knowledge and propaganda becomes increasingly (2)______. This metamorphosis is not merely technological but ontological, reshaping how individuals perceive their agency. The citizen morphs into a data node, his behavior quantified and curated to feed predictive models of consumption and compliance. Amid this shift, traditional norms of accountability and transparency are often rendered (3)______, buried under technical jargon and opaque algorithms. Efforts to reclaim civic integrity must contend with this techno-political apparatus that simultaneously empowers and ensnares.

For those committed to revitalizing public discourse, the challenge lies in cultivating (4)______ practices-ones that resist the homogenizing tendencies of digital systems. Rather than acquiesce to algorithmic flattening, democratic actors must foreground plurality and dissent, embracing complexity over coherence. In this regard, ethical resistance becomes not an act of rebellion but of (5)______, an assertion of human interpretive agency against machinic determinism.

What should come in the place of blank number 1? [Steno 15 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Blank (1) needs a verb meaning the contours are being erased/diminished. Effaced (wiped out) fits: democratic deliberation is being steadily effaced.

Option meanings
emblazoned — displayed brightly
effaced — erased, wiped out [मिटाया गया]
extolled — praised
exacerbated — worsened

The context (supplanted by platforms) supports “effaced”.

In contrast to earthquakes or wars, other violence is insidious, playing itself out over decades smog, poisoned water, eroded soil. These are not shocks but creeping disasters. Such damage has been described as "slow violence," not because it is less profound, but because it is less spectacular. It does not have the dramatic images that grab the public eye. It is therefore frequently (1)______ in media reporting, policy action, and public debate.

This invisibility is not an accident. Economies that profit from such destruction spend a lot on public relations, lobbying, and research camouflage. They present agony as the byproduct of progress or a technical glitch and not as systemic neglect. Agony is reported to victims as having no connection, their contexts misinterpreted. This repetitive denial (2)______ the very possibility for acknowledgment.

What makes slow violence so insidious is its unequal distribution. It hurts most those who have the least political power-rural poor, indigenous peoples, urban minorities. The privileged will never lay eyes on the toxins, but the marginalized inhale them. Without so much as a mention of this violence, resistance will continue to be fragmented and justice delayed. It takes more than policy to solve it-it takes a new kind of attention: slow noticing, slow journalism, slow solidarity. These are not positions of passivity but radical acts of care. They (3)______ the rhythms of harm and provide room for grief, witness, and repair.

Most legal systems are, however, constructed to address the spectacular, rather than the smoldering. At the point when damage is apparent, accountability mechanisms usually have not worked. question.en:
In contemporary cognitive science, human judgment is increasingly understood as a product of layered neural and psychological mechanisms rather than a purely rational calculus. Decisions that appear deliberate are often (A) by unconscious biases that subtly recalibrate perception before conscious deliberation even begins. This recognition has significantly undermined earlier models of rational agency, suggesting instead that cognition is dynamically constructed in real time.
Within this framework, behavioural economists argue that heuristics, while computationally efficient, can (B) systematic errors in probabilistic reasoning, particularly under conditions of uncertainty and informational overload. Such errors are not incidental but structurally embedded within the architecture of human cognition.
Clinical psychology has similarly evolved, with therapeutic paradigms increasingly encouraging individuals to (C) entrenched cognitive schemas rather than merely suppressing symptomatic expressions of distress. This shift reflects an understanding that maladaptive thought patterns are self-reinforcing and resistant to superficial correction.
Neuroscientific evidence further indicates that the brain (D) capable of extensive functional reorganization, even in adulthood, thereby challenging earlier assumptions about fixed neural circuitry. This adaptability underpins many modern rehabilitative and psychotherapeutic interventions.
Nevertheless, scholars caution that public discourse often (E) complex psychological constructs into overly simplistic explanatory frames, thereby obscuring the nuanced interplay between cognition, emotion, and environment.
Fill in the blank (A) with the correct word. [Selection Post (Graduate) 17 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

question.en:
Electric vehicles (EVs) promise lower emissions, quieter cities, and reduced dependence on fossil fuels. However, the transition to electric mobility requires substantial investment in charging infrastructure, reliable electricity grids, and sustainable battery production. (A) ________ policymakers must recognize that technological innovation alone cannot guarantee widespread adoption. Although EVs reduce tailpipe emissions, irresponsible mining practices may (B) ________ ecological degradation in resource-rich regions if environmental safeguards remain inadequate. Such confidence may encourage manufacturers to expand production and reduce prices. Equally important is the creation of an (D) ________ that rewards innovation without discouraging fair competition. Long-term industrial growth also depends on institutional credibility and predictable governance.
Ultimately, the success of electric mobility will be determined by society's willingness to invest (E) ________ a comprehensive transition that balances environmental responsibility, economic practicality, and social equity.
Identify the correct discourse marker for blank (A). [Selection Post (Graduate) 19 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

question.en:
In increasingly interdependent ecosystems, trust is no longer a soft virtue but a strategic asset that determines institutional resilience. While many organizations profess commitment to transparency, such declarations often fail to (A) under scrutiny when operational opacity persists beneath performative disclosure. Moreover, stakeholders are increasingly unwilling to (B) rhetorical assurances, particularly when prior breaches of confidence have not been adequately redressed. This skepticism is further amplified in digital environments where information asymmetry and rapid dissemination of partial narratives distort institutional intent. In such contexts, leaders must (C) reputational capital with caution, as overextension of goodwill may precipitate a rapid erosion of legitimacy. Nevertheless, trust deficits, once entrenched, do not easily (D) through cosmetic reforms or episodic outreach initiatives. Such dynamics underscore the importance of aligning formal governance structures with informal norms of accountability. Consequently, reputational repair requires sustained behavioral consistency rather than episodic signaling exercises that merely project responsiveness without substantive change. Therefore, institutions that consistently align incentives with ethical imperatives are more likely to (E) enduring legitimacy across shifting socio-political landscapes. Without such alignment, even well-designed frameworks risk gradual erosion of stakeholder confidence.
Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank (A). [Selection Post (Graduate) 22 Sep 2026 Shift 1]

question.en:
Complete the following passage by filling in the blanks with the most appropriate words from the options given below.
Oceanic literature has long been obscured by Western perspectives that view the sea as a vast, empty void between "significant" landmasses. In the imperial imagination, the ocean was (A)________ a highway for trade or a barrier to be conquered. This "terra-centric" view effectively erased the complex histories and cultures of the peoples who lived upon and with the water.
Modern Pacific writers, however, are reclaiming this space, asserting that the ocean is a connector (B)________ than a divider. They describe the sea not as a desert of salt, but as a "sea of islands" interconnected by ancient voyaging routes. This shift in perspective transforms the ocean from a site of transit into a site of profound cultural belonging and identity.
Had the early colonial cartographers respected the indigenous seafaring traditions and navigational charts, the maps of today might look very different. Instead of vast blue expanses labelled as "unexplored", we would see a web of ancestral pathways. The refusal to acknowledge these traditions was a deliberate act of (C)________ silencing that facilitated colonial expansion.
Though these narratives are often marginalised in global literary curricula, they provide a vital counter-history antithetical (D)________ the standard tales of discovery. They challenge the idea that history only happens on land. By centring the ocean, these authors force us to reconsider the fluidity of borders and the permanence of cultural ties.
Their prose is often (E)________ with metaphors of fluidity and currents, challenging the rigid, static borders imposed by imperial powers. This literature does not just tell a story; it performs an act of decolonisation. It reminds us that for those who call the ocean home, the water is the most solid ground they know.
Fill in the blank (A) with an adverb that indicates a diminished viewpoint in this context. [Selection Post (12th) 16 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

In the imperial imagination, the ocean was (A)________ a highway for trade or a barrier to be conquered. This "terra-centric" view effectively erased the complex histories and cultures of the peoples who lived upon and with the water.
Modern Pacific writers, however, are reclaiming this space, asserting that the ocean is a connector (B)________ than a divider. They describe the sea not as a desert of salt, but as a "sea of islands" interconnected by ancient voyaging routes. This shift in perspective transforms the ocean from a site of transit into a site of profound cultural belonging and identity.
Had the early colonial cartographers respected the indigenous seafaring traditions and navigational charts, the maps of today might look very different. Instead of vast blue expanses labelled as "unexplored", we would see a web of ancestral pathways. The refusal to acknowledge these traditions was a deliberate act of (C)________ silencing that facilitated colonial expansion.
Though these narratives are often marginalised in global literary curricula, they provide a vital counter-history antithetical (D)________ the standard tales of discovery. They challenge the idea that history only happens on land. By centring the ocean, these authors force us to reconsider the fluidity of borders and the permanence of cultural ties.
Their prose is often (E)________ with metaphors of fluidity and currents, challenging the rigid, static borders imposed by imperial powers. This literature does not just tell a story; it performs an act of decolonisation. It reminds us that for those who call the ocean home, the water is the most solid ground they know.
Fill in the blank (E) with a word that means that metaphors are spread through every part of the writing. [Selection Post (12th) 16 Sep 2026 Shift 2]

solution.en:
Meaning: Suffused means gradually spread through or over; permeated. In this context, it accurately describes prose that is permeated throughout with metaphors of fluidity.
Other options:
• Interspersed: Scattered among or between other things.
• Conflated: Combined two or more sets of information/texts into one.
• Attenuated: Reduced in force, effect, or value; weakened.
